questions.stem: In a club, 20% of the members are in fifth grade. There are 8 fifth graders. How many members does the club have?
questions.solution: 20% is one fifth of the members, so the club has $8\times 5=40$ members.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: A shirt is on sale for 10% off. That saves 3 dollars. What was the shirt's price before the sale, in dollars?
questions.solution: The 3 dollars saved is 10%, or one tenth, of the price. The price was $3\times 10=30$ dollars.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: 75% of a number is 30. What is 25% of the same number?
questions.solution: 75% is 3 times 25%. So 25% of the number is $30\div 3=10$.

questions.stem: A plant is 40 cm tall. It grows by 10%. How tall is it now, in centimeters?
questions.solution: 10% of 40 is 4, so the plant is $40+4=44$ cm tall.

questions.stem: A shirt that costs 50 dollars is 20% off. What is the sale price in dollars?
questions.solution: 20% of 50 is 10 dollars. The sale price is $50-10=40$ dollars. (30 comes from taking away 20 dollars instead of 20%.)

questions.stem: A town has 200 people. The number of people goes up by 25%. How many people are there now?
questions.solution: 25% of 200 is 50. Now there are $200+50=250$ people.

questions.stem: A price falls from 80 dollars to 60 dollars. By what percent did the price decrease? Give the number only.
questions.solution: The price fell by 20 dollars. $\frac{20}{80}=\frac{1}{4}=25\%$ of the old price.

questions.stem: A price rises from 10 dollars to 12 dollars. What is the percent increase?
questions.solution: The price rose by 2 dollars. Compared with the old price, $\frac{2}{10}=\frac{20}{100}$, a 20% increase.

questions.stem: A number starts at 100. It goes up by 10%. Then the new number goes up by 10%. What is the final number?
questions.solution: After the first rise: $100+10=110$. The second rise is 10% of 110, which is 11. The final number is $110+11=121$.

questions.stem: An 80-dollar item is 50% off in a sale. Then the sale price is taken 50% off again. What is the final price in dollars?
questions.solution: The first sale makes it $80\div 2=40$ dollars. The second makes it $40\div 2=20$ dollars. (Two 50% cuts do not make 100%.)

questions.stem: Mia has 100 dollars in savings. In one year it grows by 50%. In the next year the new amount grows by 10%. How many dollars does she have after the two years?
questions.solution: After year one: $100+50=150$ dollars. In year two it grows by 10% of 150, which is 15. Total: $150+15=165$ dollars.

questions.stem: A toy costs 10 dollars. Its price is raised by 100%. Then the new price is lowered by 50%. What is the final price in dollars?
questions.solution: A 100% rise doubles 10 to 20 dollars. A 50% cut then halves 20 to 10 dollars.

questions.stem: Sam puts 200 dollars in a bank that pays 5% simple interest per year. How many dollars of interest does he earn in 1 year?
questions.solution: 5% of 200 is $200\div 100\times 5=10$ dollars.

questions.stem: Simple interest of 4% per year is paid on 100 dollars. How many dollars of interest is paid over 3 years?
questions.solution: Each year the interest is 4 dollars. Over 3 years: $4\times 3=12$ dollars.

questions.stem: A 300-dollar loan charges simple interest of 10% per year. How many dollars of interest does it charge over 2 years?
questions.solution: Each year the interest is 10% of 300, which is 30 dollars. Over 2 years: $30\times 2=60$ dollars.

questions.stem: Mia puts 300 dollars in an account paying 10% simple interest per year and leaves it for 2 years. How many dollars are in the account at the end?
questions.solution: The interest each year is 30 dollars, so over 2 years it is 60 dollars. The account holds $300+60=360$ dollars.

questions.stem: $\frac{7}{20}$ is the same as ?%. What number is the ?
Which of these is equal to 0.045?
questions.solution: Multiply by 100 to get the percent: $0.045\times 100=4.5$, so 0.045 is 4.5%.

questions.stem: Write $12\frac{1}{2}\%$ as a decimal.
$\frac{3}{8}$ of a race is finished. What percent of the race is finished?
What is 15% of 80?
What is 35% of 60?
A restaurant bill is 64 dollars. A 15% tip is added. How many dollars is the tip?
questions.solution: 10% of 64 is 6.4 and 5% is 3.2. The tip is $6.4+3.2=9.6$ dollars.

questions.stem: What is $12.5\%$ of 96?
What is 150% of 40?
questions.solution: 150% is one and a half times the number: $40+20=60$.

questions.stem: A school has 480 students. 35% ride the bus and 25% walk. The rest are driven by their families. How many students are driven?
questions.solution: $35\%+25\%=60\%$ travel by bus or on foot, so 40% are driven. 10% of 480 is 48, so 40% is $4\times 48=192$.

questions.stem: 15 is what percent of 12? Give the number only.
questions.solution: $\frac{15}{12}=1.25=125\%$. A percent can be more than 100 when the part is bigger than the whole you compare with.

questions.skill: Finding what percent one number is of another
questions.stem: A quiz has 25 questions. Tom missed 6 of them. What percent of the questions did he get right?
questions.solution: He got $25-6=19$ right. $\frac{19}{25}=\frac{76}{100}$, which is 76%. (24% is the percent he missed.)

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: 30% of a number is 18. What is the number?
questions.solution: 10% of the number is $18\div 3=6$, so the whole number is $6\times 10=60$.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: A jacket's price is reduced by 12 dollars. This is 15% of the original price. What was the original price in dollars?
questions.solution: 5% is $12\div 3=4$ dollars, so 100% is $4\times 20=80$ dollars.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: In a school, 54 girls are 45% of all the students. How many students does the school have?
questions.solution: 5% is $54\div 9=6$ students, so 100% is $6\times 20=120$ students.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: After a 20% raise, Sam earns 36 dollars an hour. How many dollars an hour did Sam earn before the raise?
questions.solution: The new pay is 120% of the old pay. 120% = 36, so 10% = 3 and 100% = 30 dollars.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: The sale price after 25% off is 45 dollars. What was the price before the sale, in dollars?
questions.solution: The sale price is 75% of the old price, so 25% is $45\div 3=15$ and 100% is $15\times 4=60$ dollars.

questions.stem: A phone costs 250 dollars. Its price drops by 18%. What is the new price in dollars?
questions.solution: 18% of 250 is 45 dollars. The new price is $250-45=205$ dollars.

questions.stem: A number goes from 40 to 52. Which statement is true?
questions.solution: The change is $52-40=12$. Compared with the starting value 40, $\frac{12}{40}=\frac{30}{100}$, so it is a 30% increase.

questions.stem: The rent goes from 800 dollars to 860 dollars. What is the percent increase? Give the number only.
questions.solution: The rent rose by 60 dollars. $\frac{60}{800}=0.075=7.5\%$.

questions.stem: A shirt was 45 dollars and is now 36 dollars. By what percent was the price reduced? Give the number only.
questions.solution: The price fell by 9 dollars. $\frac{9}{45}=\frac{1}{5}=20\%$.

questions.stem: A store raises the price of a 25-dollar item by 8%. What is the new price in dollars?
questions.solution: 8% of 25 is 2 dollars. The new price is $25+2=27$ dollars.

questions.stem: A price of 200 dollars goes up by 50%. Then the new price goes down by 50%. What is the final price in dollars?
questions.solution: The rise gives $200+100=300$ dollars. The fall is 50% of 300, which is 150, so the final price is $300-150=150$ dollars.

questions.stem: A number is increased by 10%. Then the result is decreased by 10%. How does the final number compare with the starting number?
questions.solution: Start with 100. After +10% it is 110. A 10% decrease takes off 11, leaving 99. That is 1% lower than 100.

questions.stem: A 60-dollar jacket is 25% off. Then the sale price gets an extra 20% off. What is the final price in dollars?
questions.solution: After 25% off: $60-15=45$ dollars. An extra 20% of 45 is 9, so the final price is $45-9=36$ dollars.

questions.stem: A town has 4000 people. The number grows by 20% in one year, and then by 10% in the next year. How many people live in the town after the two years?
questions.solution: After year one: $4000+800=4800$. Year two adds 10% of 4800, which is 480. The total is $4800+480=5280$.

questions.stem: A bond of 800 dollars pays 3% simple interest every year. How many dollars of interest has it paid after 4 years?
questions.solution: Each year: 3% of 800 is 24 dollars. Over 4 years: $24\times 4=96$ dollars.

questions.stem: Sara borrows 1500 dollars at 6% simple interest per year for 2 years. How many dollars does she pay back in all?
questions.solution: Each year the interest is 6% of 1500, which is 90 dollars. Over 2 years: 180 dollars. She pays back $1500+180=1680$ dollars.

questions.stem: A 2000 dollar deposit earns 90 dollars of simple interest in 1.5 years. What is the yearly interest rate, as a percent? Give the number only.
questions.solution: In one year it earns $90\div 1.5=60$ dollars. $\frac{60}{2000}=0.03=3\%$.

questions.stem: Rosa wants her savings to earn 60 dollars of interest. She has 500 dollars in an account that pays 4% simple interest each year. For how many years must she leave the money in?
questions.solution: Each year the interest is 4% of 500, which is 20 dollars. $60\div 20=3$ years.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers has the greatest value?
questions.solution: As decimals: $\frac{5}{8}=0.625$; 0.6; 62% is 0.62; $\frac{7}{12}\approx 0.583$. The greatest is $\frac{5}{8}$.

questions.stem: 0.0375 is the same as ?%. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Multiply by 100 to change a decimal to a percent: $0.0375\times 100=3.75$.

questions.stem: Which percent is equal to $\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{4}$?
What is 40% of 25% of 200?
questions.solution: 25% of 200 is 50. Then 40% of 50 is 20.

questions.stem: 30% of 70 is the same as what percent of 30? Give the number only.
questions.solution: 30% of 70 is 21. And 21 is $\frac{21}{30}=0.7$ of 30, which is 70%. (In general, a% of b equals b% of a.)

questions.stem: A school has 600 students and 45% of them are boys. Of the boys, 20% play chess. How many boys play chess?
questions.solution: The boys number 45% of 600, which is 270. Then 20% of 270 is 54.

questions.stem: A mixture of 8 liters is 25% acid and the rest is water. How many liters of water must be added so that the mixture is 20% acid?
questions.solution: The acid is 25% of 8, which is 2 liters, and it stays 2 liters. For 2 liters to be 20%, the whole mixture must be $2\div 0.2=10$ liters. So add $10-8=2$ liters of water.

solve.work: acid 2 L; 2/0.2=10 L total; add 2 L water

questions.stem: A store has 80 shirts. 35% are red. Half of the shirts that are not red are blue. How many shirts are neither red nor blue?
questions.solution: 35% of 80 is 28 red shirts, so 52 are not red. Half of 52 is 26 blue, so $52-26=26$ are neither red nor blue.

questions.solution: The cake is 1000 grams. $\frac{250}{1000}=\frac{25}{100}$, which is 25%.

questions.skill: Finding what percent one number is of another
questions.stem: Of 60 students, 24 have a pet. Of the students who have a pet, 18 have a dog. What percent of ALL 60 students have a dog? Give the number only.
questions.solution: The question compares 18 with all 60 students, not with the 24 pet owners. $\frac{18}{60}=\frac{30}{100}$, which is 30%.

questions.skill: Finding what percent one number is of another
questions.stem: A team has won 18 of its first 30 games. It has 20 games left. How many of those 20 games must it win to have won exactly 60% of all 50 games?
questions.solution: 60% of 50 is 30 wins in all. It already has 18, so it needs $30-18=12$ more wins.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: 20% of a number plus 30% of the same number is 45. What is the number?
questions.solution: 20% + 30% = 50% of the number, so half of the number is 45 and the number is 90.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: A bike is 15% off and its sale price is 51 dollars. What was the price before the discount, in dollars?
questions.solution: The sale price is 85% of the old price. 85% = 51, so 1% = 0.6 and 100% = 60 dollars.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: A rope is used in two steps: first 40% of its length is used, then 25% of what is left is used. 18 meters remain. How many meters long was the rope at the start?
questions.solution: After the first step 60% is left. After using 25% of that, 75% of 60% is left, which is 45% of the rope. If 45% of the rope is 18 m, then 5% is 2 m and the rope is 40 m.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent
questions.stem: 120% of a number is 66. What is 50% of that number?
questions.solution: 10% of the number is $66\div 12=5.5$. So the number is 55 and half of it is 27.5.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a percent

A price goes up from 36 dollars to 45 dollars. Then it falls back to 36 dollars. By what percent did it fall from 45 dollars? Give the number only.
questions.solution: It fell by 9 dollars from 45. $\frac{9}{45}=\frac{1}{5}=20\%$. (The rise from 36 was 25%, a different percent.)

questions.stem: A town's population falls from 2400 to 2100. What is the percent decrease?
questions.solution: The drop is 300. Compared with the old population, $\frac{300}{2400}=\frac{1}{8}=12.5\%$.

questions.stem: After an 8% raise, Ana earns 5400 dollars a month. How many dollars a month did she earn before the raise?
questions.solution: The new pay is 108% of the old pay. 108% = 5400, so 1% = 50 and 100% = 5000 dollars.

questions.stem: By what percent must a price of 80 dollars be increased to become 130 dollars? Give the number only.
questions.solution: The increase is 50 dollars. $\frac{50}{80}=0.625=62.5\%$.

questions.stem: A 100-dollar item is reduced by 20% to 80 dollars. By what percent must the new price be increased to get back to 100 dollars?
questions.solution: The new price must rise by 20 dollars. Compared with 80 dollars, $\frac{20}{80}=25\%$. (It is not 20%, because the 20 dollars is now compared with a smaller price.)

questions.stem: An 80-dollar coat is 30% off. Then a 10% sales tax is added to the sale price. What is the total cost in dollars?
questions.solution: 30% off makes the price $80\times 0.7=56$ dollars. The 10% tax is 5.6 dollars, so the total is $56+5.6=61.6$ dollars.

questions.stem: A store takes 20% off a price and then takes 30% off the new price. This is the same as one discount of what percent?
questions.solution: Start with 100. After 20% off: 80. Then 30% of 80 is 24, leaving 56. The total taken off is $100-56=44$, which is 44%.

questions.stem: A price goes up by 25%. By what percent must the new price then be lowered to get back to the original price? Give the number only.
questions.solution: Start with 100. After the 25% rise it is 125. To get back to 100 we take off 25, and $\frac{25}{125}=20\%$.

questions.stem: A town has 500 people. Its population grows by 20% each year for 2 years. What is the population after the 2 years?
questions.solution: After year one: $500+100=600$. Year two adds 20% of 600, which is 120. Total: $600+120=720$. (The second 20% is of the new, larger number.)

questions.stem: A 1000-dollar bike is given three 10% discounts in a row, each taken from the price left by the one before. What is the final price in dollars?
questions.solution: Each discount multiplies the price by 0.9: $1000\times 0.9=900$, then $810$, then $729$ dollars.

questions.stem: A price is raised by 10%, then raised by 10% again, then lowered by 20%. How does the final price compare with the starting price?
questions.solution: Start with 100. After +10%: 110. After +10%: 121. A 20% cut takes off 24.2, leaving 96.8. That is 3.2% lower than 100.

questions.stem: After 5 years at 4% simple interest per year, an account holds 1200 dollars in all. How many dollars were put in at the start?
questions.solution: In 5 years the interest is $5\times 4\%=20\%$ of the starting amount. So 120% of the starting amount is 1200 and the starting amount is 1000 dollars.

questions.stem: At a certain yearly rate of simple interest, an amount of money doubles in 20 years. What is the yearly rate?
questions.solution: To double, the interest must equal the starting amount (100%). Over 20 years that is $100\div 20=5\%$ each year.

questions.stem: Jin puts 2500 dollars at 4% simple interest per year for 2 years, and 1500 dollars at 6% simple interest per year for 3 years. How many dollars of interest does Jin earn in all?
questions.solution: First amount: $2500\times 0.04\times 2=200$ dollars. Second amount: $1500\times 0.06\times 3=270$ dollars. Total: $200+270=470$ dollars.

questions.stem: A 600 dollar loan costs 54 dollars of simple interest over 18 months. What is the yearly interest rate, as a percent? Give the number only.
questions.solution: 18 months is 1.5 years, so one year costs $54\div 1.5=36$ dollars. $\frac{36}{600}=0.06=6\%$.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{144}$?
questions.solution: $12\times 12=144$, so the square root of 144 is 12.

questions.stem: Which number is equal to $\sqrt{49}$?
questions.solution: $7\times 7=49$, so $\sqrt{49}=7$. Doubling, halving or squaring 49 does not give a square root.

questions.stem: Maya thinks of a positive whole number. When she multiplies it by itself she gets 169. What is her number?
questions.solution: $13\times 13=169$, so her number is 13.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is a perfect square?
questions.solution: $8\times 8=64$, so 64 is a perfect square. Whole numbers multiplied by themselves never give 48, 72 or 80.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{1}+\sqrt{100}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{1}=1$ and $\sqrt{100}=10$, so the sum is $1+10=11$.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: What is $(\sqrt{17})^2$?
questions.solution: Squaring undoes a square root, so $(\sqrt{17})^2=17$.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{5^2}$?
questions.solution: $5^2=25$ and $\sqrt{25}=5$. The square root undoes the square.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: Which is equal to $\sqrt{9}\times\sqrt{9}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{9}=3$, so the product is $3\times 3=9$.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: Suppose $n^2=64$ and $n$ is positive. What is $n$?
Which is the same as $\sqrt{12}$?
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 12: 12 = 4 × 3. Then $\sqrt{12}=\sqrt{4}\times\sqrt{3}=2\sqrt{3}$.

questions.stem: Write $\sqrt{18}$ in simplest form.
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 18: 18 = 9 × 2. Then $\sqrt{18}=\sqrt{9}\times\sqrt{2}=3\sqrt{2}$.

questions.stem: Sam wants to simplify $\sqrt{20}$. Which answer is correct and fully simplified?
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 20: 20 = 4 × 5. Then $\sqrt{20}=\sqrt{4}\times\sqrt{5}=2\sqrt{5}$.

questions.stem: A square has an area of 27 square centimeters. Which gives the length of its side, in centimeters, in simplest form?
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 27: 27 = 9 × 3. Then $\sqrt{27}=\sqrt{9}\times\sqrt{3}=3\sqrt{3}$.

questions.stem: Write $\sqrt{8}$ in simplest form.
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 8: 8 = 4 × 2. Then $\sqrt{8}=\sqrt{4}\times\sqrt{2}=2\sqrt{2}$.

questions.stem: Which is the same as $\sqrt{45}$?
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 45: 45 = 9 × 5. Then $\sqrt{45}=\sqrt{9}\times\sqrt{5}=3\sqrt{5}$.

questions.stem: Between which two whole numbers is $\sqrt{20}$?
questions.solution: $4^2=16$ and $5^2=25$. Since 20 is between 16 and 25, $\sqrt{20}$ is between 4 and 5.

questions.stem: $\sqrt{40}$ is between which two whole numbers?
questions.solution: $6^2=36$ and $7^2=49$. 40 is between 36 and 49, so $\sqrt{40}$ is between 6 and 7.

questions.stem: What is the largest whole number that is less than $\sqrt{30}$?
questions.solution: $5^2=25$ and $6^2=36$, so $\sqrt{30}$ is between 5 and 6. The largest whole number below it is 5.

solve.work: 25<30<36, sqrt30 about 5.48; largest whole number below is 5.

questions.stem: What is the smallest whole number that is greater than $\sqrt{10}$?
questions.solution: $3^2=9$ and $4^2=16$, so $\sqrt{10}$ is between 3 and 4. The smallest whole number above it is 4.

solve.work: 9<10<16, sqrt10 about 3.16; smallest whole number above is 4.

questions.stem: Which whole number is closest to $\sqrt{26}$?
questions.solution: $5^2=25$ is very close to 26, while $6^2=36$ is far away. So $\sqrt{26}$ is just a little more than 5.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is between 3 and 4?
questions.solution: $3^2=9$ and $4^2=16$, so we need a number whose square is between 9 and 16. Only 12 is. $\sqrt{5}$ is about 2, $\sqrt{20}$ is about 4.5 and $\sqrt{30}$ is about 5.5.

solve.work: 9<12<16 so sqrt12 is between 3 and 4; sqrt30~5.5, sqrt20~4.5, sqrt5~2.2.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A square has an area of 64 square centimeters. How long is one side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = side × side, and $8\times 8=64$. The side is 8 cm.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A square tile has sides of 11 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = side × side = $11\times 11=121$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A square rug has an area of 36 square feet. Which could be the length of one side?
questions.solution: $6\times 6=36$, so each side is 6 feet. The other lengths are 36 divided by 4, 3 and 2, which is not how sides work.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A square floor is covered with 49 square tiles in equal rows. How many tiles are in each row?
questions.solution: The tiles make a square, so the number in a row times itself is 49. $7\times 7=49$.

solve.work: 49 tiles in a square array: 7 rows of 7.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: Which square has an area of 25 square centimeters?
choices: A square with sides of 12.5 centimeters
A square with sides of 5 centimeters
A square with sides of 50 centimeters
A square with sides of 625 centimeters
questions.answer: A square with sides of 5 centimeters
questions.solution: $5\times 5=25$, so the sides are 5 centimeters. The others come from halving, doubling or squaring 25.

solve.answer: A square with sides of 5 centimeters

questions.stem: Which number is the greatest?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{40}$ is about 6.3, $\sqrt{20}$ is about 4.5, and the others are 5 and 4. So $\sqrt{40}$ is greatest. ($5^2=25<40$.)

questions.stem: Which number is the least?
questions.solution: $8^2=64$ and $9^2=81$, so $\sqrt{70}$ is between 8 and 9, which is less than 9. $\sqrt{90}$ is between 9 and 10. So $\sqrt{70}$ is least.

questions.stem: How many of these numbers are greater than 3: $\sqrt{4}$, $\sqrt{9}$, $\sqrt{16}$, $\sqrt{25}$?
questions.solution: The numbers are 2, 3, 4 and 5. Only 4 and 5 are greater than 3, so the answer is 2.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{4}\times\sqrt{9}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{4}=2$ and $\sqrt{9}=3$, so the product is $2\times 3=6$.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{8}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{8}=\sqrt{2\times 8}=\sqrt{16}=4$.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$?
questions.solution: A square root times itself gives the number under the root, so $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}=3$.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{25}+\sqrt{16}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{25}=5$ and $\sqrt{16}=4$, so the sum is 9. (Note it is not $\sqrt{41}$.)

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{\frac{9}{25}}$?
What is $\sqrt{0.49}$?
questions.solution: $0.7\times 0.7=0.49$, so the square root of 0.49 is 0.7.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{2^4\times 3^2}$?
questions.solution: $2^4\times 3^2=(2^2\times 3)^2$, so the square root is $2^2\times 3=12$. (Check: 16 × 9 = 144.)

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{100-36}$?
questions.solution: First subtract under the root: $100-36=64$. Then $\sqrt{64}=8$.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: If $\sqrt{n}=13$, what is $n$?
questions.solution: Squaring both sides gives $n=13^2=169$.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: How many different numbers, positive or negative, have a square equal to 121?
questions.solution: $11\times 11=121$ and $(-11)\times(-11)=121$. No other numbers work, so there are 2.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{16}=4$ and $\sqrt{9}=3$, so $\sqrt{16}+\sqrt{9}=7$. But $\sqrt{16+9}=\sqrt{25}=5$, and $\sqrt{16\times 9}=\sqrt{144}=12$.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 50 are perfect squares?
questions.solution: The perfect squares up to 50 are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36 and 49. That is 7 numbers.

questions.stem: Write $\sqrt{72}$ in simplest form.
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 72: 72 = 36 × 2. Then $\sqrt{72}=\sqrt{36}\times\sqrt{2}=6\sqrt{2}$.

questions.stem: Which is the same as $\sqrt{48}$?
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 48: 48 = 16 × 3. Then $\sqrt{48}=\sqrt{16}\times\sqrt{3}=4\sqrt{3}$.

questions.stem: Sam wants to simplify $\sqrt{98}$. Which answer is correct and fully simplified?
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 98: 98 = 49 × 2. Then $\sqrt{98}=\sqrt{49}\times\sqrt{2}=7\sqrt{2}$.

questions.stem: A square has an area of 90 square centimeters. Which gives the length of its side, in centimeters, in simplest form?
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 90: 90 = 9 × 10. Then $\sqrt{90}=\sqrt{9}\times\sqrt{10}=3\sqrt{10}$.

questions.stem: Write $\sqrt{160}$ in simplest form.
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 160: 160 = 16 × 10. Then $\sqrt{160}=\sqrt{16}\times\sqrt{10}=4\sqrt{10}$.

questions.stem: $4\sqrt{5}=\sqrt{n}$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: Move the 4 under the root by squaring it: $4\sqrt{5}=\sqrt{16\times 5}=\sqrt{80}$. So $n=80$.

questions.stem: Which of these is equal to $2\sqrt{15}$?
questions.solution: $2\sqrt{15}=\sqrt{4\times 15}=\sqrt{60}$. The others come from 2×15, 2+15 and 15 squared.

questions.stem: Between which two whole numbers is $\sqrt{75}$?
questions.solution: $8^2=64$ and $9^2=81$. 75 is between 64 and 81, so $\sqrt{75}$ is between 8 and 9.

questions.stem: $\sqrt{115}$ lies between which two consecutive integers?
questions.solution: $10^2=100$ and $11^2=121$. 115 is between them, so $\sqrt{115}$ is between 10 and 11.

questions.stem: What whole number is closest to $\sqrt{41}$?
questions.solution: $6^2=36$ and $7^2=49$. 41 is much closer to 36 than to 49, so $\sqrt{41}$ is about 6.4 and the closest whole number is 6.

questions.stem: What whole number is closest to $\sqrt{87}$?
questions.solution: $9^2=81$ and $10^2=100$. 87 is closer to 81 than to 100, so $\sqrt{87}$ is about 9.3, and the closest whole number is 9.

questions.stem: Which is the best estimate of $\sqrt{20}$?
questions.solution: $4^2=16$ and $5^2=25$. 20 is about halfway, so $\sqrt{20}$ is about 4.5 (indeed $4.5^2=20.25$).

questions.stem: A square has an area of 70 square meters. Its side is between two consecutive whole numbers of meters. What is the larger one?
questions.solution: $8^2=64$ and $9^2=81$, so the side $\sqrt{70}$ is between 8 and 9. The larger is 9.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A square has an area of 81 square inches. What is the distance around it, in inches?
questions.solution: The side is $\sqrt{81}=9$ inches. The distance around is $4\times 9=36$ inches.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A square has a perimeter of 20 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each side is $20\div 4=5$ cm. The area is $5\times 5=25$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A square has an area of 48 square centimeters. Which gives the length of its side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{48}=\sqrt{16\times 3}=4\sqrt{3}$. Dividing 48 by 4 gives 12, but that is the wrong idea.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: Pam walks once around the edge of a square field whose area is 400 square meters. How many meters does she walk?
questions.solution: The side is $\sqrt{400}=20$ meters. She walks $4\times 20=80$ meters.

questions.stem: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{15}$ is about 3.9, then 4, then $\sqrt{20}$ is about 4.5, then 5. So the order is $\sqrt{15}$, 4, $\sqrt{20}$, 5.

questions.stem: Which whole number is between $\sqrt{30}$ and $\sqrt{40}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{30}$ is about 5.5 and $\sqrt{40}$ is about 6.3. The only whole number between them is 6 ($6^2=36$, and 36 is between 30 and 40).

questions.stem: How many whole numbers are greater than $\sqrt{20}$ and less than $\sqrt{50}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{20}$ is about 4.5 and $\sqrt{50}$ is about 7.1. The whole numbers between are 5, 6 and 7, which is 3 numbers.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{12}\times\sqrt{3}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{12}\times\sqrt{3}=\sqrt{36}=6$.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{50}\div\sqrt{2}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{50}\div\sqrt{2}=\sqrt{50\div 2}=\sqrt{25}=5$.

questions.stem: $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{6}$ is equal to which of these?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{6}=\sqrt{12}=\sqrt{4\times 3}=2\sqrt{3}$.

questions.stem: Marta has a ribbon $3\sqrt{5}$ meters long and gets another $2\sqrt{5}$ meters. How many meters does she have in all?
questions.solution: Add the numbers in front, like adding 3 apples and 2 apples: $3+2=5$, so the sum is $5\sqrt{5}$.

questions.stem: A path is made of two straight parts, one $\sqrt{8}$ meters long and one $\sqrt{2}$ meters long. How long is the whole path, in meters?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}$, so the sum is $2\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{2}=3\sqrt{2}$.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{2^6\times 5^2}$?
questions.solution: $2^6\times 5^2=(2^3\times 5)^2$, so the root is $2^3\times 5=8\times 5=40$.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{1.44}$?
questions.solution: $1.2\times 1.2=1.44$, so the answer is 1.2.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{4\times 9\times 25\times 16}$?
questions.solution: The root of a product is the product of the roots: $2\times 3\times 5\times 4=120$.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: If $\sqrt{x+3}=5$, what is $x$?
questions.solution: Squaring both sides, $x+3=25$, so $x=22$. Check: $\sqrt{25}=5$.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: A positive number is equal to 4 times its own square root. What is the number?
questions.solution: Let the number be n. Then $n=4\sqrt{n}$. Dividing by $\sqrt{n}$ gives $\sqrt{n}=4$, so $n=16$. Check: $4\times\sqrt{16}=16$.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.solution: The sum is 64 (the first 8 odd numbers add to $8^2$). Check: 1+3=4, +5=9, +7=16, +9=25, +11=36, +13=49, +15=64. So the root is 8.

solve.work: Sum of first 8 odd numbers = 64; sqrt=8.

questions.skill: Squares and square roots as opposites
questions.stem: For how many whole numbers $n$ from 1 to 100 is $\sqrt{n}$ also a whole number?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{n}$ is a whole number only when n is a perfect square: $1^2, 2^2, \ldots, 10^2$. That is 10 numbers.

questions.stem: Write $\sqrt{450}$ in simplest form.
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 450: 450 = 225 × 2. Then $\sqrt{450}=\sqrt{225}\times\sqrt{2}=15\sqrt{2}$.

questions.stem: Which is the same as $\sqrt{1100}$?
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 1100: 1100 = 100 × 11. Then $\sqrt{1100}=\sqrt{100}\times\sqrt{11}=10\sqrt{11}$.

questions.stem: Sam wants to simplify $\sqrt{600}$. Which answer is correct and fully simplified?
questions.solution: Find the biggest perfect square that divides 600: 600 = 100 × 6. Then $\sqrt{600}=\sqrt{100}\times\sqrt{6}=10\sqrt{6}$.

questions.stem: Simplify $\sqrt{2^5\times 3^3}$.
questions.solution: $2^5\times 3^3=2^4\times 3^2\times 2\times 3=144\times 6$. So the root is $12\sqrt{6}$.

questions.stem: $\sqrt{n}=6\sqrt{5}$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: $6\sqrt{5}=\sqrt{36\times 5}=\sqrt{180}$, so $n=180$.

questions.stem: How many positive whole numbers $n$ with $n\le 50$ make $\sqrt{n}$ equal to $a\sqrt{2}$ for some positive whole number $a$?
questions.solution: We need $n=2a^2$: for a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 that gives 2, 8, 18, 32, 50. Next would be 72, which is too big. So there are 5.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers are between $\sqrt{20}$ and $\sqrt{80}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{20}$ is about 4.5 and $\sqrt{80}$ is about 8.9. The whole numbers between are 5, 6, 7 and 8, so there are 4.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers are greater than $\sqrt{50}$ and less than $\sqrt{200}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{50}$ is about 7.1 ($7^2=49$) and $\sqrt{200}$ is about 14.1 ($14^2=196$). The whole numbers 8 to 14 fit, which is 7 numbers.

questions.stem: What is the largest whole number $n$ for which $\sqrt{n}<7.5$?
questions.solution: We need $n<7.5^2=56.25$. The largest whole number below 56.25 is 56.

questions.stem: What is the smallest whole number $n$ for which $\sqrt{n}>11.5$?
questions.solution: We need $n>11.5^2=132.25$. The smallest whole number above 132.25 is 133.

questions.stem: Between which two whole numbers is $3\sqrt{10}$?
questions.solution: $3\sqrt{10}=\sqrt{9\times 10}=\sqrt{90}$. Since $9^2=81$ and $10^2=100$, it is between 9 and 10.

questions.stem: Between which two whole numbers is $2+\sqrt{17}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{17}$ is between 4 and 5 ($16<17<25$), so adding 2 gives a number between 6 and 7.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A square has an area of 98 square centimeters. What is the length of its side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{98}=\sqrt{49\times 2}=7\sqrt{2}$.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A rectangle is 8 cm wide and 18 cm long. A square has the same area. How long is each side of the square, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The rectangle's area is $8\times 18=144$. The square's side is $\sqrt{144}=12$ cm.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A square has a perimeter of 36 units. A rectangle that is 3 units wide has the same area as the square. How long is the rectangle, in units?
questions.solution: The square's side is $36\div 4=9$, so its area is 81. The rectangle's length is $81\div 3=27$.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A square has sides of $5\sqrt{3}$ centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = side × side = $5\sqrt{3}\times 5\sqrt{3}=25\times 3=75$.

questions.skill: Square roots in squares: side and area
questions.stem: A small square has sides of 6 cm. A big square has twice the area. What is the side of the big square, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The small area is 36, so the big one is 72. Its side is $\sqrt{72}=\sqrt{36\times 2}=6\sqrt{2}$. (Doubling the area does not double the side.)

questions.stem: Which of these four numbers has the largest value?
questions.solution: Put each under one root: $5\sqrt{2}=\sqrt{50}$, $4\sqrt{3}=\sqrt{48}$, $3\sqrt{5}=\sqrt{45}$, $2\sqrt{10}=\sqrt{40}$. The biggest is $\sqrt{50}$, which is $5\sqrt{2}$.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is NOT between 7 and 8?
questions.solution: $7^2=49$ and $8^2=64$, so a number between 7 and 8 has a square between 49 and 64. 50, 55 and 60 are; 70 is not.

questions.stem: How many of $\sqrt{10}$, $\sqrt{20}$, $\sqrt{30}$, $\sqrt{40}$ and $\sqrt{50}$ are greater than 5?
questions.solution: $5^2=25$. A root is greater than 5 when the number under it is greater than 25: that is 30, 40 and 50. So 3.

questions.stem: For how many positive whole numbers $n$ is $\sqrt{n}<3\sqrt{2}$?
questions.solution: $3\sqrt{2}=\sqrt{18}$, so we need $n<18$. The numbers 1 to 17 work, so there are 17.

questions.stem: Which number is closest to $\sqrt{50}$?
questions.solution: $7^2=49$ and $7.1^2=50.41$, so $\sqrt{50}$ is about 7.07. That is closest to 7.1.

questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{18}+\sqrt{50}-\sqrt{8}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}$, $\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt{2}$, $\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}$. So the total is $3+5-2=6$ copies of $\sqrt{2}$: $6\sqrt{2}$.

questions.stem: What is $(3\sqrt{2})(2\sqrt{6})$?
questions.solution: Multiply the front numbers: $3\times 2=6$. Multiply the roots: $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{6}=\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt{3}$. So the answer is $6\times 2\sqrt{3}=12\sqrt{3}$.

questions.stem: A rectangle is $\sqrt{12}$ cm long and $\sqrt{27}$ cm wide. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{12}\times\sqrt{27}=\sqrt{12\times 27}=\sqrt{324}=18$. (Or $2\sqrt{3}\times 3\sqrt{3}=6\times 3=18$.)
$(2\sqrt{3})^2=4\times 3=12$ and $(3\sqrt{2})^2=9\times 2=18$. The sum is 30.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: Which angle is a right angle?
questions.solution: A right angle is a quarter of a full turn: $360\div 4=90$ degrees.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: An angle measures $130^\circ$. What kind of angle is it?
questions.solution: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees, a right angle is exactly 90, and an obtuse angle is between 90 and 180. 130 is between 90 and 180, so it is obtuse.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: How many degrees are in a straight angle?
questions.solution: A straight angle is a straight line, which is half of a full turn: 180 degrees.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: A spinner turns one quarter of the way around a full turn. Through how many degrees does it turn?
questions.solution: A full turn is 360 degrees, and $360\div 4=90$.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: Which angle is acute?
questions.solution: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees. Only 15 degrees is less than 90.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: An angle of $180^\circ$ is called a
questions.solution: Its two sides make one straight line, so it is a straight angle. A right angle is 90 degrees and a full turn is 360 degrees.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: A door swings open through $40^\circ$, and then it swings another $25^\circ$. How many degrees has it swung in all?
questions.solution: Add the two swings: $40+25=65$ degrees.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: The minute hand of a clock goes all the way around in 60 minutes. Through how many degrees does it move in 15 minutes?
questions.solution: 15 minutes is a quarter of 60 minutes, so the hand moves a quarter of 360 degrees: $360\div 4=90$.

questions.stem: Two angles are complementary. One is $30^\circ$. How many degrees is the other?
questions.solution: Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. $90-30=60$.

questions.stem: What is the complement of an angle of $72^\circ$? Answer in degrees.
Which two angles are complementary?
questions.solution: Complementary angles add to 90. $40+50=90$. The other pairs add to 180 or 120.

questions.stem: Complementary angles add up to how many degrees?
questions.solution: Complementary angles make a right angle together, so they add up to 90 degrees.

questions.stem: Two equal angles are complementary. How many degrees is each one?
questions.solution: Together they make 90 degrees, so each is $90\div 2=45$.

questions.stem: The complement of $20^\circ$ is

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: Two angles are supplementary. One is $100^\circ$. How many degrees is the other?
questions.solution: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees. $180-100=80$.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: Two angles sit side by side on a straight line. One is $110^\circ$. How many degrees is the other?
questions.solution: Angles on a straight line add up to 180. $180-110=70$.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: What is the supplement of $65^\circ$?
questions.solution: $180-65=115$. (25 is the complement, and 295 is 360-65.)

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: Supplementary angles add up to how many degrees?
questions.solution: Supplementary angles together make a straight line, which is 180 degrees.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: Which two angles are supplementary?
questions.solution: Supplementary angles add to 180. $70+110=180$. The others add to 90, 140 and 360.

questions.stem: Two straight lines cross. One of the four angles is $50^\circ$. How many degrees is the angle directly across from it?
questions.solution: The angles directly across from each other when two lines cross are vertical angles, and they are equal.

questions.stem: Vertical angles are always
questions.solution: Two straight lines crossing make two pairs of vertical angles, and each pair is equal.

questions.stem: Two lines cross. One of the angles is $70^\circ$. Another angle next to it (sharing a side, so that together they make a straight line) is how many degrees?
questions.solution: Angles next to each other on a line add to 180. $180-70=110$.

questions.stem: Which describes parallel lines?
choices: Lines that meet at a right angle
Lines that cross at exactly one point
Lines that have the same length
Lines in the same flat surface that never meet
questions.answer: Lines in the same flat surface that never meet
questions.solution: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet, however far they go.

solve.answer: Lines in the same flat surface that never meet

questions.stem: A line crosses two parallel lines. Two corresponding angles are equal. One of them is $65^\circ$. How many degrees is the other?
questions.solution: Corresponding angles formed by a line crossing parallel lines are equal, so the other is 65 degrees too.

questions.stem: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. Alternate interior angles are
questions.solution: When the lines are parallel, alternate interior angles are equal.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles of $50^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. How many degrees is the third angle?
questions.solution: The three angles add up to 180. $50+60=110$ and $180-110=70$.

questions.stem: A right triangle has one acute angle of $35^\circ$. How many degrees is the other acute angle?
questions.solution: The right angle is 90, so the other two angles add up to $180-90=90$. $90-35=55$.

questions.stem: Every angle of an equilateral triangle is the same size. How many degrees is each angle?
questions.solution: The angles add up to 180, so each is $180\div 3=60$.

questions.stem: The three angles of any triangle add up to
questions.solution: The angles of every triangle add up to 180 degrees.

questions.stem: A triangle has two equal angles of $50^\circ$ each. How many degrees is the third angle?
The four angles of any quadrilateral add up to
questions.solution: A quadrilateral can be cut into two triangles, and 2 × 180 = 360.

questions.stem: Every angle of a square is the same size. How many degrees is each angle?
questions.solution: The four angles add up to 360, so each is 90 degrees.

questions.stem: Three angles of a quadrilateral are $90^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $100^\circ$. How many degrees is the fourth angle?

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: An angle measures $250^\circ$. What kind of angle is it?
questions.solution: An angle bigger than 180 degrees and less than 360 degrees is a reflex angle.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: The hour hand of a clock moves from pointing at the 3 to pointing at the 7. Through how many degrees does it turn?
questions.solution: The 12 hours share a full turn of 360 degrees, so each hour is $360\div 12=30$ degrees. From 3 to 7 is 4 hours: $4\times 30=120$ degrees.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: A skater spins three quarters of a full turn. Through how many degrees does she spin?
questions.solution: A quarter turn is 90 degrees, and $3\times 90=270$.

questions.stem: One of two complementary angles is twice as big as the other. How many degrees is the bigger one?
questions.solution: The two angles are 1 part and 2 parts, 3 parts in all, and they make 90 degrees. One part is 30, so the bigger angle is $2\times 30=60$.

questions.stem: The complement of an angle is $25^\circ$. What is the supplement of that angle?
questions.solution: The angle is $90-25=65$ degrees. Its supplement is $180-65=115$.

questions.stem: Two complementary angles measure $(x+20)^\circ$ and $(x+30)^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: They add to 90: $2x+50=90$, so $2x=40$ and $x=20$. The angles are 40 and 50 degrees.

questions.stem: Which angle is equal to its own complement?
questions.solution: We need an angle x with $x+x=90$, so $x=45$.

questions.stem: An angle is $12^\circ$ more than its complement. How many degrees is the angle?
questions.solution: Together the angle and its complement make 90. If the angle is 12 more, then $90+12=102$ is twice the angle, so the angle is 51. Check: the complement is 39 and $39+12=51$.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: Two supplementary angles are such that one is 3 times as big as the other. How many degrees is the smaller one?
questions.solution: The parts are 1 and 3, 4 parts in all, making 180. One part is $180\div 4=45$.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: Three angles sit side by side on a straight line. Two of them are $40^\circ$ and $65^\circ$. How many degrees is the third?
questions.solution: The three angles add up to 180. $40+65=105$ and $180-105=75$.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: What is the supplement of $128^\circ$?

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: An angle is $20^\circ$ less than its supplement. How many degrees is the angle?
questions.solution: The angle and its supplement add to 180. If the supplement is 20 more than the angle, then $180-20=160$ is twice the angle, so the angle is 80. Check: the supplement is 100.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: Angle P is $40^\circ$. Angle Q is the complement of P. Angle R is the supplement of Q. How many degrees is R?
Two lines cross. A pair of vertical angles measure $(2x+10)^\circ$ and $(3x-5)^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal, so $2x+10=3x-5$. Then $x=15$. Each angle is 40 degrees.

questions.stem: Two lines cross. One of the four angles is 3 times as big as an angle next to it. How many degrees is the smaller of the two?
questions.solution: Two angles next to each other add to 180. With parts 1 and 3, one part is $180\div 4=45$.

solve.work: Adjacent angles are supplementary: x+3x=180, x=45.

questions.stem: Two lines cross and make four angles. One angle is $40^\circ$. How many degrees do the other three angles add up to?
questions.solution: The four angles make a full turn, 360 degrees. $360-40=320$.

questions.stem: Two lines cross and make four angles. Which statement must be true?
choices: Any two angles that are side by side add up to 180 degrees
Any two angles that are side by side are equal
questions.answer: Any two angles that are side by side add up to 180 degrees
questions.solution: Two side-by-side angles together make a straight line, so they add to 180. The four angles are not all equal unless the lines meet at right angles.

solve.answer: Any two angles that are side by side add up to 180 degrees
solve.work: Adjacent angles form a straight line, sum 180. Not all equal/acute in general.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Which statement is always true?
choices: Two interior angles on the same side are equal
Alternate interior angles add up to 180 degrees
Vertical angles add up to 180 degrees
questions.solution: Corresponding angles are equal. Interior angles on the same side add to 180 (they are equal only if both are 90), alternate interior angles are equal, and vertical angles are equal.

solve.work: Corresponding angles are equal; others false.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two angles lie between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal. One of them is $110^\circ$. How many degrees is the other?
questions.solution: Interior angles on the same side of the transversal add to 180. $180-110=70$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two angles lie between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal (alternate interior angles). One of them is $75^\circ$. How many degrees is the other?
questions.solution: Alternate interior angles are equal, so the other is 75 degrees.

questions.stem: A transversal cuts two parallel lines and makes 8 angles. One of the angles is $55^\circ$. How many of the 8 angles measure $55^\circ$?
questions.solution: The 55-degree angle has three partners equal to it: its vertical angle, and the two matching angles at the other line. That makes 4 angles of 55 degrees. The other 4 angles measure 125 degrees.

solve.work: Four angles equal 55 (two at each intersection), the other four are 125. Answer 4.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two corresponding angles measure $(x+15)^\circ$ and $(2x-25)^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Corresponding angles are equal: $x+15=2x-25$. Adding 25 and subtracting x gives $x=40$. Each angle is 55 degrees.

questions.stem: A transversal cuts two parallel lines and makes 8 angles, four acute and four obtuse. An acute angle measures $55^\circ$. How many degrees is an obtuse angle?
questions.solution: An acute angle and an obtuse angle next to each other make a straight line. $180-55=125$.

questions.stem: The angles of a triangle measure $x^\circ$, $2x^\circ$ and $3x^\circ$. How many degrees is the smallest angle?
questions.solution: $x+2x+3x=6x=180$, so $x=30$. The smallest angle is 30 degrees.

questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of $40^\circ$. Its other two angles are equal. How many degrees is each of them?
questions.solution: The two equal angles share $180-40=140$, so each is $140\div 2=70$.

questions.stem: One exterior angle of a triangle is $120^\circ$. One of the two inside angles that are not next to it is $50^\circ$. How many degrees is the other one of those two?
questions.solution: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two inside angles that are not next to it. $120-50=70$.

solve.work: Exterior = sum of the two remote interior angles: 120-50=70.

questions.stem: Can a triangle have angles of $60^\circ$, $70^\circ$ and $60^\circ$?
choices: No, a triangle cannot have two equal angles
No, they add up to 190 degrees
Yes, every angle is less than 90 degrees
Yes, two of the angles are equal
questions.answer: No, they add up to 190 degrees
questions.solution: The angles of a triangle must add to 180, but $60+70+60=190$.

solve.answer: No, they add up to 190 degrees

questions.stem: A right triangle has two acute angles, and one is twice as big as the other. How many degrees is the smaller one?
questions.solution: The two acute angles add to 90, in parts 1 and 2. One part is $90\div 3=30$.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the angles of a hexagon, in degrees?
questions.solution: A hexagon can be cut into $6-2=4$ triangles, so the angles add to $4\times 180=720$.

questions.stem: What is each angle of a regular pentagon, in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles add to $3\times 180=540$, and there are 5 equal angles: $540\div 5=108$.

questions.stem: The angles of a polygon add up to 900 degrees. How many sides does it have?
questions.solution: A polygon with n sides has angles adding to $(n-2)\times 180$. $900\div 180=5$, so $n-2=5$ and $n=7$.

questions.stem: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is $40^\circ$. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.solution: The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360 degrees. $360\div 40=9$ sides.

questions.stem: What is each angle of a regular octagon, in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles add to $6\times 180=1080$, and there are 8 equal angles: $1080\div 8=135$.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: At exactly 4:00, the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock make an angle. How many degrees is the smaller angle between them?
questions.solution: The 12 hour marks are spread around 360 degrees, so each hour is 30 degrees. At 4:00 the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand at 4, which is $4\times 30=120$ degrees apart.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: At exactly 3:30, the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock make an angle. How many degrees is the smaller angle between them?
questions.solution: Each hour is 30 degrees. The minute hand points at 6, which is 180 degrees from 12. The hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4, which is $3.5\times 30=105$ degrees from 12. The difference is $180-105=75$.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: At exactly 2:20, the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock make an angle. How many degrees is the smaller angle between them?
questions.solution: The minute hand points at 4, which is $4\times 30=120$ degrees from 12. The hour hand has moved past 2 by a third of an hour: $60+10=70$ degrees from 12. The difference is $120-70=50$.

questions.skill: Angle measures, turns and kinds of angles
questions.stem: Four angles fit exactly around a point. Three of them are $90^\circ$, $110^\circ$ and $75^\circ$. How many degrees is the fourth?
questions.solution: Angles around a point make a full turn, 360 degrees. $90+110+75=275$ and $360-275=85$.

questions.stem: An angle is $6^\circ$ less than 3 times its complement. How many degrees is the angle?
questions.solution: Let the angle be a. Its complement is $90-a$. So $a=3(90-a)-6=264-3a$, which gives $4a=264$ and $a=66$. Check: the complement is 24, and $3\times 24-6=66$.

questions.stem: Two complementary angles differ by $20^\circ$. How many degrees is the bigger angle?
questions.solution: If the bigger angle is 20 more than the smaller, then bigger + bigger = $90+20=110$, so the bigger angle is 55 degrees (and the smaller is 35).

questions.stem: The supplement of an angle is 3 times its complement. How many degrees is the angle?
questions.solution: Let the angle be a. Then $180-a=3(90-a)=270-3a$, so $2a=90$ and $a=45$. Check: supplement 135, complement 45, and $3\times 45=135$.

questions.stem: The supplement of an angle is $30^\circ$ more than twice its complement. How many degrees is the angle?
questions.solution: Let the angle be a. Then $180-a=2(90-a)+30=210-2a$, so $a=30$. Check: supplement 150, complement 60, and $2\times 60+30=150$.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: Two supplementary angles are such that one is 4 times the other. How many degrees is the smaller angle?
questions.solution: The angles are 1 part and 4 parts, 5 parts in all, making 180. One part is $180\div 5=36$.

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: Three angles on a straight line measure $x^\circ$, $2x^\circ$ and $3x^\circ$. How many degrees is the smallest of them?

questions.skill: Supplementary angles and angles on a line
questions.stem: Two supplementary angles are in the ratio 2 to 7. How many degrees is the bigger angle?
questions.solution: There are $2+7=9$ parts making 180 degrees, so a part is 20 degrees. The bigger angle is $7\times 20=140$.

questions.stem: Three straight lines cross at one point and make six angles around it. Going around the point, the angles are $a^\circ, b^\circ, c^\circ, a^\circ, b^\circ, c^\circ$ in turn. If $a=35$ and $b=60$, what is $c$?
questions.solution: Three angles side by side on one side of a line make a straight line: $a+b+c=180$. So $c=180-35-60=85$.

questions.stem: Two lines cross. A pair of vertical angles measure $(4x+15)^\circ$ and $(6x-25)^\circ$. How many degrees is an angle that is next to one of them?
questions.solution: Vertical angles are equal: $4x+15=6x-25$, so $x=20$. Each of them is $4\times 20+15=95$ degrees. An angle next to it is $180-95=85$.

questions.stem: Two lines cross. One angle measures $(3x+12)^\circ$ and an angle next to it measures $(2x+3)^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Angles next to each other add to 180: $5x+15=180$, so $5x=165$ and $x=33$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two interior angles on the same side of the transversal measure $(3x+10)^\circ$ and $(2x+30)^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Interior angles on the same side add to 180: $5x+40=180$, so $5x=140$ and $x=28$. The angles are 94 and 86 degrees.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two corresponding angles measure $(5x-20)^\circ$ and $(3x+10)^\circ$. How many degrees is each of these angles?
questions.solution: Corresponding angles are equal: $5x-20=3x+10$, so $2x=30$ and $x=15$. Each angle is $3\times 15+10=55$ degrees.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two alternate interior angles measure $(4x)^\circ$ and $(x+60)^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Alternate interior angles are equal: $4x=x+60$, so $3x=60$ and $x=20$. Each angle is 80 degrees.

questions.stem: A transversal cuts two parallel lines and makes 8 angles. Four of the angles are 55 degrees and the other four are 125 degrees. What do all 8 angles add up to, in degrees?
questions.solution: $4\times 55=220$ and $4\times 125=500$, and $220+500=720$. (Each crossing point has 360 degrees of angles, and there are 2 of them.)

questions.stem: A transversal cuts two parallel lines and makes 8 angles. One of the angles is $70^\circ$. How many of the 8 angles measure $110^\circ$?
questions.solution: Four angles match the 70-degree angle (the same size). The other four are next to them on straight lines, so each is 110 degrees.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Which pair of angles must add up to 180 degrees?
choices: Two angles between the lines, on the same side of the transversal
questions.answer: Two angles between the lines, on the same side of the transversal
questions.solution: Interior angles on the same side of the transversal are supplementary. Corresponding, alternate interior and vertical angles are equal pairs (they add to 180 only when all are 90 degrees).

solve.answer: Two angles between the lines, on the same side of the transversal

questions.stem: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 to 3 to 4. How many degrees is the largest angle?
questions.solution: There are $2+3+4=9$ parts making 180 degrees, so a part is 20. The largest angle is $4\times 20=80$.

questions.stem: The angles of a triangle measure $x^\circ$, $(x+10)^\circ$ and $(x+20)^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: $3x+30=180$, so $3x=150$ and $x=50$. The angles are 50, 60 and 70.

questions.stem: An exterior angle at one corner of a triangle is $110^\circ$. The two inside angles that are not next to it are in the ratio 4 to 7. How many degrees is the larger of those two?
questions.solution: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two far inside angles, so they add to 110. There are $4+7=11$ parts, each 10 degrees, so the larger is $7\times 10=70$.

solve.work: Remote interior sum = 110; 11 parts of 10; larger 70.

questions.stem: In a triangle, angle A is $20^\circ$ more than angle B, and angle C is twice angle B. How many degrees is angle B?
questions.solution: Call angle B b. Then A is $b+20$ and C is $2b$, so $b+(b+20)+2b=4b+20=180$. Then $4b=160$ and $b=40$. The angles are 60, 40 and 80.

questions.stem: What is the greatest number of obtuse angles a triangle can have?
questions.solution: An obtuse angle is more than 90 degrees. Two of them would add to more than 180, which is too much for a triangle, so at most 1 is possible (and 1 is possible, for example 100, 40, 40).

solve.work: Two obtuse angles exceed 180, so at most 1.

questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has an angle of $100^\circ$. How many degrees is each of its other two angles?
questions.solution: Two angles of 100 would already make 200, which is too many, so the 100-degree angle is the one that is alone. The other two are equal and share $180-100=80$, so each is 40.

solve.work: 100 must be the vertex angle (two 100s exceed 180): (180-100)/2=40.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the angles of a polygon with 20 sides, in degrees?
questions.solution: A polygon with 20 sides is cut into $20-2=18$ triangles, so the angles add to $18\times 180=3240$.

questions.stem: What is each angle of a regular polygon with 12 sides, in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles add to $10\times 180=1800$, and $1800\div 12=150$. (Or each exterior angle is $360\div 12=30$, and $180-30=150$.)

questions.stem: Each angle inside a regular polygon is $156^\circ$. How many sides does it have?
questions.solution: Each exterior angle is $180-156=24$ degrees. The exterior angles add to 360, so there are $360\div 24=15$ sides.

questions.stem: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is $36^\circ$. What do the angles inside the polygon add up to, in degrees?
questions.solution: $360\div 36=10$ sides. The inside angles add to $(10-2)\times 180=1440$.

questions.stem: Four angles of a pentagon are $100^\circ$, $110^\circ$, $120^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. How many degrees is the fifth angle?
questions.solution: The angles of a pentagon add to $3\times 180=540$. $100+110+120+90=420$, and $540-420=120$.

questions.stem: The four angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 1 to 2 to 3 to 4. How many degrees is the largest angle?
questions.solution: There are $1+2+3+4=10$ parts making 360 degrees, so a part is 36. The largest angle is $4\times 36=144$.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: A garden is a rectangle 9 meters long and 4 meters wide. What is its perimeter, in meters?
questions.solution: The perimeter is the distance around: $9+4+9+4=26$ meters.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangular card is 12 centimeters long and 5 centimeters wide. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area is length times width: $12\times 5=60$ square centimeters. (34 is the perimeter and 17 is the sum of the two sides.)

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: The area of a rectangle is 48 square inches and its width is 6 inches. How many inches long is it?
questions.solution: Area = length $\times$ width, so length = $48\div 6=8$ inches.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: Which rectangle has a perimeter of 20 centimeters?
questions.solution: The perimeter is twice (length + width). For length 7 and width 3 it is $2\times(7+3)=20$. The others give 22, 22 and 24.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: Each side of a square sign is 7 centimeters long. What is the perimeter of the sign, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A square has 4 equal sides: $4\times 7=28$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: A square tile has sides of 9 inches. What is its area, in square inches?
questions.solution: Area of a square = side $\times$ side $=9\times 9=81$ square inches.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: A square garden has a perimeter of 36 meters. How long is one side, in meters?
questions.solution: The four sides are equal, so one side is $36\div 4=9$ meters.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: Which square has a perimeter of 24 centimeters?
choices: A square with sides of 4 cm
A square with sides of 12 cm
A square with sides of 6 cm
A square with sides of 8 cm
questions.answer: A square with sides of 6 cm
questions.solution: The perimeter of a square is 4 times its side. Since $4\times 6=24$, the sides are 6 cm.

solve.answer: A square with sides of 6 cm

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 10 centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = $\frac12\times$ base $\times$ height $=\frac12\times 10\times 6=30$.

questions.stem: A triangular garden bed has a base of 8 meters and a height of 5 meters. What is its area, in square meters?
questions.solution: Area = $\frac12\times 8\times 5=20$ square meters. (40 forgets to halve.)

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 24 square centimeters and a base of 8 centimeters. What is its height, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Base $\times$ height is twice the area: $48$. So the height is $48\div 8=6$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 7 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = base $\times$ height $=7\times 5=35$.

questions.stem: A parallelogram-shaped rug has a base of 10 feet and a height of 4 feet. What is its area, in square feet?
questions.solution: Area = $10\times 4=40$ square feet. (20 would be half, as for a triangle.)

questions.stem: A parallelogram has an area of 48 square centimeters and a base of 8 centimeters. What is its height, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Height = area $\div$ base $=48\div 8=6$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 6 centimeters and a height of 4 centimeters. A rectangle 6 centimeters wide has the same area. How long is the rectangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The parallelogram has area $6\times 4=24$. The rectangle has width 6, so its length is $24\div 6=4$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 6 centimeters and 10 centimeters, and a height of 4 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = $\frac12\times(6+10)\times 4=32$.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 5 meters and 9 meters, and a height of 6 meters. What is its area, in square meters?
questions.solution: Area = $\frac12\times(5+9)\times 6=42$. (84 forgets to halve.)

questions.stem: A trapezoid has an area of 40 square centimeters and parallel sides of 7 centimeters and 3 centimeters. What is its height, in centimeters?
questions.solution: $\frac12\times(7+3)\times h=40$, so $5h=40$ and $h=8$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: A circular pool has a diameter of 18 meters. What is its radius, in meters?
questions.solution: The radius is half the diameter: $18\div 2=9$ meters.

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: A circle has a radius of 5 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area $=\pi r^2=\pi\times 5^2=25\pi$. ($10\pi$ is the circumference.)

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: A circle has a diameter of 9 centimeters. What is its circumference, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Circumference $=\pi\times$ diameter $=9\pi$.

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: A round plate has a diameter of 10 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is the circumference of the plate, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Circumference $=\pi\times 10\approx 3.14\times 10=31.4$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
questions.stem: A shape is made from a rectangle 8 centimeters long and 3 centimeters wide, and a square with sides of 2 centimeters joined to it. They do not overlap. What is the total area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The rectangle has area $8\times 3=24$. The square has area $2\times 2=4$. The total is $24+4=28$.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
questions.stem: A rectangle is 10 centimeters long and 6 centimeters wide. A square with sides of 2 centimeters is cut out of one corner. What is the area that is left, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Whole rectangle: $10\times 6=60$. Cut-out square: $2\times 2=4$. What is left: $60-4=56$.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
questions.stem: Two rectangles, each 6 centimeters long and 2 centimeters wide, are placed with their long sides touching to make one bigger rectangle. What is the perimeter of the bigger rectangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The new rectangle is 6 centimeters long and $2+2=4$ centimeters wide. Its perimeter is $2\times(6+4)=20$.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
questions.stem: A rectangle is 12 centimeters long and 5 centimeters wide. A straight cut parallel to the short sides divides it into two equal pieces. What is the area of each piece, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The whole rectangle has area $12\times 5=60$. Two equal pieces each have half of it: 30.

questions.stem: A floor is covered with tiles. Which unit measures how much floor the tiles cover?
questions.solution: Covering a flat surface is area, which is measured in square units such as square meters.

solve.work: Area is measured in square units.

questions.stem: How many square tiles, each 1 centimeter on a side, are needed to cover a card that is 6 centimeters long and 5 centimeters wide?
questions.solution: There are 5 rows of 6 tiles: $5\times 6=30$ tiles.

questions.stem: A square and an equilateral triangle (a triangle with 3 equal sides) each have a perimeter of 12 centimeters. How long is one side of the triangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The triangle has 3 equal sides: $12\div 3=4$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 2 cm by 8 cm. A square has sides of 4 cm. Which statement is true?
choices: They have the same area, but the rectangle has the greater perimeter.
They have the same perimeter, but the square has the greater area.
They have the same area and the same perimeter.
The square has the greater area and the greater perimeter.
questions.answer: They have the same area, but the rectangle has the greater perimeter.
questions.solution: Areas: $2\times 8=16$ and $4\times 4=16$, equal. Perimeters: $2\times(2+8)=20$ and $4\times 4=16$. The rectangle has the greater perimeter.

solve.answer: They have the same area, but the rectangle has the greater perimeter.
solve.work: Rect: A 16, P 20. Square: A 16, P 16. Same area, rectangle larger perimeter.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: A path is 12 meters long and 2 meters wide. It is covered with paving slabs. What is the area of the path, in square meters?
questions.solution: Area $=12\times 2=24$ square meters.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: One cup of paint covers 1 square meter of wall. A rectangular wall is 5 meters long and 3 meters high. How many cups of paint cover the wall once?
questions.solution: The area of the wall is $5\times 3=15$ square meters, so 15 cups are needed.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: Carpet costs 4 dollars for each square meter. A rectangular room is 5 meters long and 3 meters wide. How many dollars does it cost to carpet the whole floor?
questions.solution: The floor has area $5\times 3=15$ square meters. The cost is $15\times 4=60$ dollars.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangular field has a perimeter of 54 meters. It is 17 meters long. How many meters wide is it?
questions.solution: Half the perimeter is length + width: $54\div 2=27$. So the width is $27-17=10$ meters.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: The length of a rectangle is 3 times its width, and its perimeter is 48 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: If the width is $w$, the perimeter is $2(w+3w)=8w=48$, so $w=6$ and the length is 18. The area is $6\times 18=108$.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangular poster is 1.5 meters long and 0.8 meter wide. What is its area, in square meters?
questions.solution: Area = $1.5\times 0.8=1.2$ square meters.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: Rectangle P is 8 cm by 3 cm. Rectangle Q is 6 cm by 5 cm. How many more square centimeters of area does Q have than P?
questions.solution: P has area $8\times 3=24$. Q has area $6\times 5=30$. The difference is $30-24=6$.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: A square courtyard has an area of 81 square meters. What is its perimeter, in meters?
questions.solution: The side is 9 meters because $9\times 9=81$. The perimeter is $4\times 9=36$ meters.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: A square has a perimeter of 20 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each side is $20\div 4=5$ centimeters. The area is $5\times 5=25$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: A runner jogs twice around a square field. Each side of the field is 120 meters long. How many meters does the runner jog?
questions.solution: One lap is $4\times 120=480$ meters. Two laps are $2\times 480=960$ meters.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of 9 centimeters and 12 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The legs of a right triangle are a base and a height. Area $=\frac12\times 9\times 12=54$.

questions.stem: A triangle has a side of 14 centimeters. The height drawn to that side is 12 centimeters. The other two sides are 13 centimeters and 15 centimeters long. What is the area of the triangle, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Use the side of 14 as the base and the height 12: area $=\frac12\times 14\times 12=84$. The other side lengths are not needed.

questions.stem: The base of a triangle is twice its height. The area of the triangle is 36 square units. How long is the base?
questions.solution: If the height is $h$, the base is $2h$ and the area is $\frac12\times 2h\times h=h^2$. So $h^2=36$, $h=6$ and the base is 12.

questions.stem: Which triangle has the greatest area?
questions.solution: Compare base $\times$ height: $63$, $60$, $56$ and $55$. The greatest is base 9 and height 7, with area 31.5 square centimeters.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 9 centimeters, a slanted side of 6 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area is base times height, not base times the slanted side: $9\times 5=45$ square centimeters.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has an area of 84 square meters and a height of 7 meters. A rectangle has the same base as the parallelogram and a height of 3 meters. What is the area of the rectangle, in square meters?
questions.solution: The base is $84\div 7=12$ meters. The rectangle has area $12\times 3=36$ square meters.

questions.stem: A field shaped like a parallelogram has a base of 25 meters and a height of 16 meters. One bag of seed covers 100 square meters. How many bags are needed to cover the whole field once?
questions.solution: The area is $25\times 16=400$ square meters. One bag covers 100, so $400\div 100=4$ bags.

questions.stem: Which parallelogram has the greatest area?
questions.solution: The areas are $6\times 7=42$, $8\times 5=40$, $10\times 4=40$ and $5\times 8=40$. The greatest is 42.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has an area of 54 square centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. One of its parallel sides is 11 centimeters long. How long is the other parallel side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The two parallel sides add to $54\times 2\div 6=18$. The other side is $18-11=7$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A garden bed is a trapezoid. Its two parallel sides are 12 meters and 20 meters long, and they are 9 meters apart. What is its area, in square meters?
questions.solution: Area $=\frac12\times(12+20)\times 9=16\times 9=144$ square meters.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has a height of 8 centimeters. Its two parallel sides together are 25 centimeters long. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area $=\frac12\times 25\times 8=100$ square centimeters.

questions.stem: Trapezoid R has parallel sides of 3 cm and 9 cm and a height of 5 cm. Trapezoid S has parallel sides of 4 cm and 8 cm and a height of 5 cm. Which statement is true?
choices: R and S have the same area.
R has twice the area of S.
questions.answer: R and S have the same area.
questions.solution: R: $\frac12\times 12\times 5=30$. S: $\frac12\times 12\times 5=30$. The parallel sides add to 12 in both, so the areas are equal.

solve.answer: R and S have the same area.

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: A round clock has a diameter of 12 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The radius is 6 centimeters. Area $=\pi\times 6^2=36\pi$.

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: The circumference of a circle is $20\pi$ meters. What is its radius, in meters?
questions.solution: Circumference $=2\pi r=20\pi$, so $r=10$ meters.

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: The area of a circle is $49\pi$ square centimeters. What is its diameter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: $\pi r^2=49\pi$, so $r^2=49$ and $r=7$. The diameter is $2\times 7=14$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: A wheel has a radius of 30 centimeters. How far does it roll, in centimeters, during one full turn?
questions.solution: In one full turn the wheel rolls one circumference: $2\pi r=2\pi\times 30=60\pi$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
questions.stem: A picture is 20 centimeters long and 15 centimeters wide. A frame 3 centimeters wide goes all the way around the picture. What is the area of the frame itself, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The picture and frame together are $26$ by $21$, with area $546$. The picture alone is $20\times 15=300$. The frame is $546-300=246$.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
questions.stem: An L-shaped room is made by cutting a 4 meter by 3 meter rectangle out of a corner of a 10 meter by 8 meter rectangle. What is the perimeter of the L-shaped room, in meters?
questions.solution: Cutting a rectangle from a corner does not change the perimeter: the new edges replace the old ones. The perimeter is $2\times(10+8)=36$ meters.

solve.work: Corner notch keeps perimeter equal to bounding rectangle: 2(10+8) = 36.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
