questions.stem: A shape is a rectangle 10 centimeters long and 6 centimeters wide, with a half circle added on one of the 6-centimeter sides. That side is the diameter of the half circle. What is the area of the whole shape, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The rectangle has area 60. The half circle has radius 3, so its area is $\frac12\pi\times 3^2=\frac92\pi$. The total is $60+\frac92\pi$.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 24 centimeters and whole-number sides. What is the greatest area it can have, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The sides add to 12. The products are $1\times 11=11$, $2\times 10=20$, $3\times 9=27$, $4\times 8=32$, $5\times 7=35$ and $6\times 6=36$. The greatest is 36.

questions.stem: Each side of a 3 centimeter by 5 centimeter rectangle is doubled in length. How many square centimeters larger is the area of the new rectangle?
questions.solution: The old area is 15. The new rectangle is 6 by 10, with area 60. The difference is $60-15=45$.

questions.stem: Four fields all have a perimeter of 36 meters. Which one has the greatest area?
questions.solution: The areas are $81$, $72$, $56$ and $32$ square meters. For a given perimeter, the square has the greatest area.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: A rectangular floor is 5 meters long and 4 meters wide. It is covered with square tiles that are 50 centimeters on each side. How many tiles are needed?
questions.solution: The floor is 500 cm by 400 cm. Along the length there are $500\div 50=10$ tiles and along the width $400\div 50=8$ tiles. The total is $10\times 8=80$ tiles.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: A pen is built against a long straight wall, so only three sides need fencing. The two sides that touch the wall are 7 meters long, and the side opposite the wall is 12 meters long. How many meters of fence are needed?
questions.solution: Fence is needed for the two 7-meter sides and the 12-meter side: $7+7+12=26$ meters.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: A wall is 6 meters wide and 3 meters high. A window 2 meters wide and 1 meter high will not be painted. Paint costs 2 dollars for each square meter. How many dollars does it cost to paint the rest of the wall?
questions.solution: The wall has area $6\times 3=18$. The window has area $2\times 1=2$. Painted area is $16$ square meters, costing $16\times 2=32$ dollars.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: A strip of wood is 3 meters long and 40 centimeters wide. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: 3 meters is 300 centimeters. The area is $300\times 40=12{,}000$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangle has whole-number sides, a perimeter of 30 centimeters and an area of 56 square centimeters. How long, in centimeters, is its longer side?
questions.solution: The two sides add up to 15. Whole numbers with product 56 are 1 and 56, 2 and 28, 4 and 14, 7 and 8. Only 7 and 8 add to 15. The longer side is 8.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangle is 5 meters by 8 meters. Both its length and its width are made 2 meters longer. By how many square meters does the area grow?
questions.solution: The old area is $5\times 8=40$. The new rectangle is 7 by 10, with area 70. The area grows by $70-40=30$.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 36 square units, and both of its sides are whole numbers. How many different perimeters can such a rectangle have? (A square counts as a rectangle.)
questions.solution: The side pairs are 1 by 36, 2 by 18, 3 by 12, 4 by 9 and 6 by 6. Their perimeters are 74, 40, 30, 26 and 24, which are 5 different values.

solve.work: Whole-number side pairs with product 36: 1x36 (P=74), 2x18 (P=40), 3x12 (P=30), 4x9 (P=26), 6x6 (P=24). Five different perimeters.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: When each side of a square is made 3 centimeters longer, the area of the square grows by 39 square centimeters. How long was each side of the original square, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Try a side of 5: the area goes from 25 to $8\times 8=64$, which is 39 more. In general the new area is $s^2+6s+9$, so $6s+9=39$ and $s=5$.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: Each side of a square is made 3 times as long. The area of the new square is how many times the area of the old square?
questions.solution: If the old side is $s$, the new side is $3s$ and the new area is $(3s)^2=9s^2$. The area is 9 times as large.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: A square piece of paper has sides of 10 centimeters. A strip 2 centimeters wide is cut off along one side, leaving a rectangle. What is the perimeter of the rectangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The rectangle left is 10 centimeters by 8 centimeters. Its perimeter is $2\times(10+8)=36$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Perimeter and area of a square
questions.stem: Two squares have areas of 25 square centimeters and 9 square centimeters. How many centimeters longer is the perimeter of the larger square than the perimeter of the smaller square?
questions.solution: The sides are 5 and 3 centimeters. The perimeters are 20 and 12, which differ by 8.

questions.stem: Triangle ABC has a base BC of 10 centimeters and an area of 60 square centimeters. Point D is on BC, 4 centimeters from B. What is the area of triangle ABD, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Triangles ABC and ABD have the same height (from A to line BC). The height is $60\times 2\div 10=12$. Triangle ABD has base 4, so its area is $\frac12\times 4\times 12=24$.

solve.work: Height = 2*60/10 = 12. ABD has base 4, same height: 24.

questions.stem: The base of a triangle is made 3 times as long, and its height is cut in half. The new area is how many times the old area?
questions.solution: Area is proportional to base $\times$ height. The new product is $3\times\frac12=\frac32$ times the old one.

questions.stem: A triangle with a base of 9 centimeters has the same area as a square whose perimeter is 24 centimeters. What is the height of the triangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The square has side $24\div 4=6$ and area 36. For the triangle, $\frac12\times 9\times h=36$, so $9h=72$ and $h=8$.

questions.stem: A triangle has corners at (0, 0), (8, 0) and (3, 6) on a grid where each unit is 1 centimeter. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Take the side from (0, 0) to (8, 0) as the base: 8 centimeters. The third corner is 6 units above it, so the height is 6. Area $=\frac12\times 8\times 6=24$.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 14 centimeters. Its base is lengthened by 6 centimeters while its height stays the same, and its area grows by 48 square centimeters. What is the height, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The extra area is the extra base times the height: $6\times h=48$, so $h=8$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 9 centimeters long and 6 centimeters wide. It is pushed over into a parallelogram with the same four side lengths. The height of the parallelogram above its 9-centimeter side is now 3 centimeters. What is the area of the parallelogram, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The area is the 9-centimeter base times the new height: $9\times 3=27$ square centimeters. It is less than the rectangle's 54.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a perimeter of 36 centimeters. One side is 10 centimeters long, and the height to that side is 6 centimeters. What is the height to the other, shorter side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The sides are 10 and 8 centimeters, because $10+8=36\div 2$. The area is $10\times 6=60$. Using the 8-centimeter side as the base, the height is $60\div 8=7.5$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has a height of 6 centimeters. Its shorter parallel side is b centimeters long and its longer parallel side is 4 centimeters longer than that. Its area is 66 square centimeters. What is b?
questions.solution: The parallel sides add to $66\times 2\div 6=22$. So $b+(b+4)=22$, $2b=18$ and $b=9$.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has two right angles. Its parallel sides are 5 centimeters and 11 centimeters, and its height is 8 centimeters. It is cut into a rectangle and a right triangle. What is the area of the triangle, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The rectangle is 5 by 8. The triangle has a base of $11-5=6$ and a height of 8, so its area is $\frac12\times 6\times 8=24$.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has an area of 90 square centimeters and a height of 9 centimeters. Its parallel sides are in the ratio 2 : 3. How long is the longer parallel side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The parallel sides add to $90\times 2\div 9=20$. Split 20 in the ratio 2 : 3: 8 and 12. The longer side is 12.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has corners at (0, 0), (10, 0), (8, 5) and (3, 5) on a grid where each unit is 1 centimeter. Its top and bottom sides are parallel. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The bottom side is 10 long. The top side runs from x = 3 to x = 8, so it is 5 long. The height is 5. Area $=\frac12\times(10+5)\times 5=37.5$.

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: A circle with radius 4 centimeters lies inside a circle with radius 7 centimeters, and the two circles have the same center. What is the area of the ring between them, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area of ring = big circle minus small circle $=49\pi-16\pi=33\pi$.

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: One circle has a circumference of $8\pi$ centimeters. A second circle has a circumference of $24\pi$ centimeters. The area of the second circle is how many times the area of the first?
questions.solution: The radii are 4 and 12, so the second radius is 3 times the first. Area grows with the square of the radius, so the second area is $3^2=9$ times as large.

questions.skill: Circumference and area of a circle
questions.stem: A circular rug has a radius of 2 meters. Rugs cost 10 dollars for each square meter. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. How many dollars does the rug cost?
questions.solution: Area $\approx 3.14\times 2^2=12.56$ square meters. The cost is $12.56\times 10=125.6$ dollars.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
questions.stem: A shape is made of five columns, each 1 centimeter wide, standing side by side on a flat base. The columns are 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 centimeters tall, from left to right. What is the perimeter of the shape, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Count the flat parts: the bottom is 5 long, and the tops of the five columns add up to 5 more, so the horizontal parts total 10. Count the upright parts: the right side is 5 tall, and the left side (1) plus the four steps up (1 each) make 5 more, so the upright parts total 10. The perimeter is $10+10=20$, the same as a 5 by 5 square.

solve.work: Staircase: perimeter equals bounding box 5 by 5: 20. (Horizontal 5+5, vertical 5 left/right total 5+5.)

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
questions.stem: A circle fits exactly inside a square with sides of 10 centimeters, touching all four sides. What is the area of the part of the square that is outside the circle, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The circle has diameter 10, so radius 5 and area $25\pi$. The square has area 100. The part outside is $100-25\pi$.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
questions.stem: A photo is 8 centimeters by 6 centimeters. It is mounted on a board so that there is a border of the same width on all four sides. The board has an area of 120 square centimeters. How wide is the border, in centimeters?
questions.solution: If the border is $x$ wide, the board is $(8+2x)$ by $(6+2x)$. Try $x=2$: $12\times 10=120$. It works, and a wider border makes the board larger than 120, a narrower one smaller, so the border is 2 centimeters.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
questions.stem: Two squares with sides of 6 centimeters and a rectangle 6 centimeters tall and 3 centimeters wide are joined in a row, side to side, to make one long rectangle. What is the perimeter of the long rectangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The long rectangle is $6+6+3=15$ wide and 6 tall. Its perimeter is $2\times(15+6)=42$. (66 adds up the three separate perimeters; 90 is the area.)

questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 60 square centimeters and whole-number sides. What is the least perimeter it can have, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The side pairs are 1 and 60, 2 and 30, 3 and 20, 4 and 15, 5 and 12, 6 and 10. The sums are 61, 32, 23, 19, 17, 16, so the perimeters are 122, 64, 46, 38, 34 and 32. The least is 32.

questions.stem: The length of a rectangle is increased by 20 percent and its width is decreased by 20 percent. What happens to the area?
questions.solution: The new area is $1.2\times 0.8=0.96$ of the old area, which is 4 percent less.

questions.stem: A rectangle and a square both have a perimeter of 40 centimeters. The rectangle is 4 centimeters longer than it is wide. How many square centimeters greater is the area of the square than the area of the rectangle?
questions.solution: The square has sides of 10 and area 100. The rectangle's sides add to 20 and differ by 4, so they are 12 and 8, with area 96. The difference is $100-96=4$.

questions.stem: One side of a rectangle is tripled and the other side stays the same. The perimeter changes from 20 centimeters to 36 centimeters. What is the area of the original rectangle, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Let the sides be $a$ (the one that is tripled) and $b$. Then $a+b=10$ and $3a+b=18$. Subtracting, $2a=8$, so $a=4$ and $b=6$. The original area is $4\times 6=24$.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: A floor is 480 centimeters long and 360 centimeters wide. It is covered with equal square tiles, with no cutting. The tiles are as large as possible. How many tiles are needed?
questions.solution: The tile side must divide both 480 and 360. The largest such number is 120. Along the length there are $480\div 120=4$ tiles and along the width $360\div 120=3$ tiles, so $4\times 3=12$ tiles.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: A rope 56 meters long is made into a rectangle with whole-number sides, using all of the rope. Which of these areas, in square meters, is NOT possible?
questions.solution: The sides add to 28. The areas are $14\times 14=196$, $11\times 17=187$ and $8\times 20=160$, all possible. The greatest possible area is 196, so 200 is not possible.

solve.work: L+W = 28. 196 = 14x14, 160 = 8x20, 187 = 11x17; 200 needs x(28-x)=200, discriminant 784-800 < 0 (also > max 196). Not possible.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: Three square pens, each with sides of 4 meters, are built in a row, touching along their sides. Fence goes around the outside of the whole row and also along each wall between pens. How many meters of fence are needed in all?
questions.solution: The whole row is $3\times 4=12$ meters long and 4 meters wide, so the outside is $2\times(12+4)=32$ meters. There are 2 walls between pens, each 4 meters: 8 more. The total is $32+8=40$.

solve.work: Outer 2(12+4) = 32, plus 2 inner walls of 4 = 8. Total 40.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter in real-life problems
questions.stem: A rectangular floor is 6 meters long and 5 meters wide. Tiles are sold in packs. Each pack covers 2.4 square meters and costs 20 dollars. Only whole packs can be bought. What is the least cost to cover the floor, in dollars?
questions.solution: The floor is 30 square meters. $30\div 2.4=12.5$, so 13 packs are needed. $13\times 20=260$ dollars.

questions.stem: The legs of a right triangle are 6 centimeters and 8 centimeters long. How long is the hypotenuse, in centimeters?
questions.solution: By the Pythagorean theorem, $6^2+8^2=36+64=100$, and $\sqrt{100}=10$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of 5 and 12. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.solution: $5^2+12^2=25+144=169$, and $\sqrt{169}=13$. (17 adds the legs; 169 forgets the square root.)

questions.stem: Ana walks 9 meters east and then 12 meters north. How many meters is she from where she started, in a straight line?
questions.solution: Her path and the straight line make a right triangle with legs 9 and 12. $9^2+12^2=81+144=225$, and $\sqrt{225}=15$ meters.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of 2 and 3. What is the length of its hypotenuse?
questions.solution: $2^2+3^2=4+9=13$, so the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{13}$.

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 10 centimeters and one leg of 6 centimeters. How long is the other leg, in centimeters?

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 and one leg of 5. What is the length of the other leg?

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: The longest side of a right triangle is 15 inches. Another side is 12 inches. How long is the third side, in inches?
questions.solution: The longest side is the hypotenuse. $15^2-12^2=225-144=81$, and $\sqrt{81}=9$ inches.

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 5 and one leg of 3. What is the length of the other leg?
questions.solution: $5^2-3^2=25-9=16$, and $\sqrt{16}=4$. (16 forgets the square root.)

questions.stem: Which set of three numbers can be the side lengths of a right triangle?
questions.solution: Check $a^2+b^2=c^2$ with the largest as $c$. $5^2+12^2=25+144=169=13^2$ works. The other sets do not.

questions.stem: A triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 is made 4 times as big in every direction. How long is its longest side?
questions.solution: Every side is multiplied by 4, so the longest side is $5\times 4=20$. (The sides 12, 16, 20 still make a right triangle.)

questions.stem: The sides of a right triangle are 10, 24 and one more number, which is the longest side. What is that number?
questions.solution: 10 and 24 are twice 5 and 12, so the longest side is twice 13: 26. Check: $100+576=676=26^2$.

questions.stem: A 45-45-90 triangle has a hypotenuse of $9\sqrt{2}$ centimeters. How long is each leg, in centimeters?
questions.solution: In a 45-45-90 triangle the hypotenuse is the leg times $\sqrt2$. So the leg is $9\sqrt2\div\sqrt2=9$ centimeters.

questions.stem: Each leg of a 45-45-90 triangle is 5 centimeters long. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.solution: The hypotenuse is the leg times $\sqrt2$, so it is $5\sqrt2$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A right triangle has two legs that are both 4 centimeters long. How many degrees is each of its other two angles?
questions.solution: Equal legs mean equal angles opposite them. The three angles add to 180 and one is 90, so the other two share 90 degrees: 45 each.

questions.stem: A square has sides of 3 centimeters. How long is its diagonal, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A diagonal cuts the square into two 45-45-90 triangles with legs 3. The hypotenuse is $3\sqrt2$ centimeters.

questions.stem: The shortest side of a 30-60-90 triangle is 5 centimeters. How long is the hypotenuse, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The hypotenuse is twice the shortest side: $2\times 5=10$ centimeters.

questions.stem: The shortest side of a 30-60-90 triangle is 4 centimeters. How long is the other leg, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The longer leg is the shortest side times $\sqrt3$: $4\sqrt3$ centimeters. (8 is the hypotenuse.)

questions.stem: The hypotenuse of a 30-60-90 triangle is 14 centimeters. How long is the shortest side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The shortest side is half the hypotenuse: $14\div 2=7$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A 10-foot ladder leans against a wall. Its foot is 6 feet from the wall. How many feet up the wall does it reach?
questions.solution: The ladder, the wall and the ground form a right triangle with hypotenuse 10 and one leg 6. The height is $\sqrt{100-36}=8$ feet.

questions.stem: A rectangular field is 24 meters long and 7 meters wide. How long is the path across the field from one corner to the opposite corner, in meters?
questions.solution: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 24 and 7. $24^2+7^2=576+49=625$, and $\sqrt{625}=25$ meters.

questions.stem: A rectangular screen is 8 inches wide and 6 inches tall. How long is its diagonal, in inches?
questions.solution: $8^2+6^2=64+36=100$, and $\sqrt{100}=10$ inches. (14 adds the sides; 28 is the perimeter.)

questions.stem: A gate is 12 feet wide and 5 feet tall. A brace runs along the diagonal from one corner to the opposite corner. How long is the brace, in feet?
Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90, 80 and 100 degrees. How many degrees is the fourth angle?
questions.solution: The four angles of a quadrilateral add to 360 degrees. The three known angles add to 270, so the fourth is $360-270=90$ degrees.

questions.stem: Which shape always has four equal sides and four right angles?
questions.solution: A rhombus has four equal sides but its angles need not be right angles. A rectangle has four right angles but its sides need not be equal. Only a square always has both.

questions.stem: One angle of a parallelogram is 70 degrees. How many degrees is an angle next to it (sharing a side)?
questions.solution: Angles next to each other in a parallelogram add to 180 degrees: $180-70=110$.

questions.stem: Which statement is true for every rectangle?
choices: All four of its sides have the same length.
Its two diagonals have the same length.
Its diagonals cross at right angles.
Only one pair of its sides is parallel.
questions.answer: Its two diagonals have the same length.
questions.solution: In a rectangle the two diagonals are equal. Sides are equal only in a square, the diagonals cross at right angles only in a square, and a rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides.

solve.answer: Its two diagonals have the same length.

questions.stem: A rhombus has diagonals of 6 centimeters and 10 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonals: $\frac12\times 6\times 10=30$.

questions.stem: A kite has diagonals of 8 centimeters and 12 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The area of a kite is half the product of its diagonals: $\frac12\times 8\times 12=48$. (96 forgets the half.)

questions.stem: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 4 centimeters and 8 centimeters, and a height of 5 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area $=\frac12\times(4+8)\times 5=30$.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 9 centimeters, a slanted side of 5 centimeters and a height of 4 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area is base times height: $9\times 4=36$. (45 uses the slanted side.)

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it called?
questions.solution: A trapezoid is a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides. The other three shapes have two pairs.

questions.stem: In a rectangle, one diagonal is 18 centimeters long. How long is the other diagonal, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length, so the other diagonal is also 18 centimeters.

questions.stem: A rhombus has a perimeter of 28 centimeters. How long is each side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A rhombus has four equal sides, so each side is $28\div 4=7$ centimeters.

questions.stem: The legs of a right triangle are 1.5 centimeters and 2 centimeters long. How long is the hypotenuse, in centimeters?
questions.solution: $1.5^2+2^2=2.25+4=6.25$, and $2.5^2=6.25$. The hypotenuse is 2.5 centimeters. (This is the 3-4-5 triangle made half as big.)

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of 4 and 6. What is the length of its hypotenuse?
questions.solution: $4^2+6^2=16+36=52$. The hypotenuse is $\sqrt{52}=\sqrt{4\times 13}=2\sqrt{13}$.

questions.stem: The legs of a right triangle are 20 centimeters and 21 centimeters long. What is the perimeter of the triangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: $20^2+21^2=400+441=841=29^2$, so the hypotenuse is 29. The perimeter is $20+21+29=70$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A square is built on each side of a right triangle. The squares on the two legs have areas of 36 square centimeters and 64 square centimeters. How long is each side of the square built on the hypotenuse, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The legs are $\sqrt{36}=6$ and $\sqrt{64}=8$ centimeters, so the hypotenuse is 10 (the area of its square is $36+64=100$, and 100 is the area, not the side).

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 29 centimeters and one leg of 20 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The other leg is $\sqrt{29^2-20^2}=\sqrt{841-400}=\sqrt{441}=21$. The area is $\frac12\times 20\times 21=210$.

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 9 and one leg of 6. What is the length of the other leg?

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has two sides of 13 centimeters and a base of 10 centimeters. How tall is the triangle, measured from the base to the opposite corner, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The height cuts the base in half, into 5 and 5. It forms a right triangle with hypotenuse 13 and one leg 5, so the height is $\sqrt{169-25}=\sqrt{144}=12$ centimeters.

questions.stem: Which set of side lengths does NOT make a right triangle?
A right triangle has sides in the ratio 5 : 12 : 13, and its perimeter is 90 centimeters. How long is its longest side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The ratio parts add to $5+12+13=30$, so one part is $90\div 30=3$ centimeters. The longest side is $13\times 3=39$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of 7, 24 and 25 centimeters. It is a right triangle. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The two shorter sides are the legs, since $7^2+24^2=625=25^2$. The area is $\frac12\times 7\times 24=84$.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of 9, 40 and 41. Which statement is true?
choices: The angle opposite the side of length 9 is a right angle.
The angle opposite the side of length 41 is a right angle.
The angle opposite the side of length 40 is a right angle.
No angle of the triangle is a right angle.
questions.answer: The angle opposite the side of length 41 is a right angle.
questions.solution: $9^2+40^2=81+1600=1681=41^2$, so the sides satisfy the Pythagorean theorem and the triangle is a right triangle. The right angle is opposite the longest side, 41.

solve.answer: The angle opposite the side of length 41 is a right angle.

questions.stem: The diagonal of a square is $10\sqrt{2}$ centimeters long. What is the area of the square, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The diagonal is the side times $\sqrt2$, so the side is 10 centimeters. The area is $10\times 10=100$.

questions.stem: The hypotenuse of a 45-45-90 triangle is 10 centimeters long. How long is each leg, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Leg $=$ hypotenuse $\div\sqrt2=\frac{10}{\sqrt2}=\frac{10\sqrt2}{2}=5\sqrt2$.

questions.stem: A right triangle has two equal legs and a hypotenuse of 12 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each leg squared is $\frac{12^2}{2}=72$ (since $\text{leg}^2+\text{leg}^2=144$). The area is $\frac12\times 72=36$.

questions.stem: The diagonal of a square is 8 centimeters long. What is the perimeter of the square, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The side is $\frac{8}{\sqrt2}=4\sqrt2$. The perimeter is $4\times 4\sqrt2=16\sqrt2$ centimeters.

questions.stem: The longer leg of a 30-60-90 triangle is $7\sqrt{3}$ centimeters. How long is the shortest side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The longer leg is the shortest side times $\sqrt3$, so the shortest side is $7\sqrt3\div\sqrt3=7$ centimeters.

questions.stem: The hypotenuse of a 30-60-90 triangle is 12 centimeters. How long is its longer leg, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The shortest side is $12\div 2=6$. The longer leg is $6\sqrt3$ centimeters.

questions.stem: The hypotenuse of a 30-60-90 triangle is 9 centimeters longer than its shortest side. How long is the hypotenuse, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The hypotenuse is twice the shortest side, so it is exactly 1 shortest side longer than it. That side is 9, and the hypotenuse is $2\times 9=18$ centimeters.

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has sides of 8 centimeters. How tall is it, measured from one side to the opposite corner, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The height cuts the triangle into two 30-60-90 triangles with hypotenuse 8. The shortest side is 4 (half the base), so the height is $4\sqrt3$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A 25-foot ladder leans against a wall and reaches 24 feet up. How many feet is the foot of the ladder from the wall?
A path goes 6 kilometers east and then 8 kilometers north. A new straight path joins the start and the end directly. How many kilometers shorter is the new path?
questions.solution: The old path is $6+8=14$ kilometers. The straight path is the hypotenuse: $\sqrt{36+64}=10$ kilometers. It is $14-10=4$ kilometers shorter.

questions.stem: A flagpole is 15 meters tall. A wire runs from the top of the pole to a point on the ground 8 meters from the base of the pole. How long is the wire, in meters?
Two angles of a parallelogram that are next to each other are in the ratio 1 : 4. How many degrees is the smaller angle?
questions.solution: Next angles add to 180 degrees. The ratio parts add to 5, so one part is $180\div 5=36$ degrees. The smaller angle is 36 degrees.

questions.stem: Which statement is true for every rhombus?
choices: Its diagonals have the same length.
All four of its angles are right angles.
Its diagonals cross at right angles.
Exactly one pair of its sides is parallel.
questions.answer: Its diagonals cross at right angles.
questions.solution: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular. They are equal only in a square, the angles are right angles only in a square, and a rhombus has two pairs of parallel sides.

solve.answer: Its diagonals cross at right angles.

questions.stem: An isosceles trapezoid has a longer base and a shorter base. The angles at the longer base are 65 degrees each. How many degrees is each angle at the shorter base?
questions.solution: Angles on the same leg of a trapezoid add to 180 degrees, because the bases are parallel. So each angle at the shorter base is $180-65=115$ degrees.

questions.stem: A square has diagonals of 10 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: A square is a rhombus, so its area is half the product of its diagonals: $\frac12\times 10\times 10=50$.

questions.stem: A rhombus has an area of 60 square centimeters, and one diagonal is 10 centimeters long. How long is the other diagonal, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Area $=\frac12 d_1 d_2$, so $\frac12\times 10\times d_2=60$, $5d_2=60$ and $d_2=12$.

questions.stem: A table top is a trapezoid. Its two parallel edges are 120 centimeters and 80 centimeters long, and they are 50 centimeters apart. What is the area of the table top, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area $=\frac12\times(120+80)\times 50=100\times 50=5000$ square centimeters.

questions.stem: A rhombus has diagonals of 12 centimeters and 16 centimeters. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The diagonals cross at right angles and cut each other in half, making right triangles with legs 6 and 8. Each side is $\sqrt{36+64}=10$, and the perimeter is $4\times 10=40$.

questions.stem: Which statement is true?
questions.solution: A square has four right angles, so it is a rectangle. A rectangle need not have equal sides, a parallelogram need not have equal sides, and a trapezoid has only one pair of parallel sides.

questions.stem: The diagonals of a rectangle cross at a point. Each diagonal is 26 centimeters long. How far is the crossing point from each corner of the rectangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and cut each other in half. The crossing point is $26\div 2=13$ centimeters from every corner.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has four equal sides and no right angles. Which name always describes it?
questions.solution: Four equal sides make it a rhombus. With no right angles it cannot be a square or a rectangle, and a rhombus has two pairs of parallel sides, so it is not a trapezoid.

questions.stem: A kite has two pairs of equal sides next to each other. Its sides are 5, 5, 9 and 9 centimeters long. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: $5+5+9+9=28$ centimeters.

questions.stem: On a coordinate grid where each unit is 1 centimeter, how many centimeters apart are the points (2, 3) and (14, 12)?
questions.solution: Going from one point to the other is 12 units across and 9 units up. These are the legs of a right triangle, so the distance is $\sqrt{12^2+9^2}=\sqrt{225}=15$.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of length $\sqrt{7}$ and 3. How long is its hypotenuse?
questions.solution: The hypotenuse squared is $(\sqrt7)^2+3^2=7+9=16$, so the hypotenuse is 4.

questions.stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 17 and a perimeter of 40. What is its area?
questions.solution: The legs add up to $40-17=23$. Also $a^2+b^2=17^2=289$. Since $(a+b)^2=a^2+b^2+2ab$, we get $529=289+2ab$, so $ab=120$. The area is half of that, 60. (The legs are 8 and 15.)

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has two sides of 17 centimeters and a base of 16 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The height splits the base into 8 and 8 and makes a right triangle with hypotenuse 17, so the height is $\sqrt{289-64}=\sqrt{225}=15$. The area is $\frac12\times 16\times 15=120$.

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: The hypotenuse of a right triangle is 10. Its two legs differ in length by 2. How long is the shorter leg?
questions.solution: Try legs 6 and 8: they differ by 2 and $6^2+8^2=36+64=100=10^2$. So the shorter leg is 6. (A leg of 8 is the longer one.)

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: Triangle ABC has a right angle at B. Side AC is 30 centimeters and side AB is 18 centimeters. What is the perimeter of the triangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: AC is the hypotenuse. $BC=\sqrt{30^2-18^2}=\sqrt{900-324}=\sqrt{576}=24$. The perimeter is $30+18+24=72$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Missing leg of a right triangle
questions.stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 41 and one leg of 9. What is the length of the other leg?

A right triangle has two sides of 12 and 16. The third side could be the hypotenuse, or it could be a leg (if 16 is the hypotenuse). What is the sum of the squares of the two possible lengths of the third side?
questions.solution: If the third side is the hypotenuse, its square is $12^2+16^2=144+256=400$. If 16 is the hypotenuse, the square of the third side is $16^2-12^2=256-144=112$. The sum is $400+112=512$.

questions.stem: How many different right triangles with whole-number side lengths have a hypotenuse of 25?
questions.solution: We need $a^2+b^2=625$ with whole numbers. The pairs are 7 and 24 ($49+576$) and 15 and 20 ($225+400$). No other pair works, so there are 2 triangles.

questions.stem: The three side lengths of a right triangle are consecutive even numbers. What is the perimeter of the triangle?
questions.solution: Call the sides $x$, $x+2$ and $x+4$. Trying small even numbers: 2, 4, 6 fail ($4+16\ne 36$), and 4, 6, 8 fail ($16+36\ne 64$), but 6, 8, 10 work ($36+64=100$). The perimeter is $6+8+10=24$.

questions.stem: The right triangles 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 7-24-25 and 9-40-41 all have whole-number sides, and in each one the hypotenuse is exactly 1 more than the longer leg. A right triangle with a shorter leg of 11 follows the same pattern. What are its longer leg and its hypotenuse?
questions.solution: If the longer leg is $b$, the hypotenuse is $b+1$, so $11^2+b^2=(b+1)^2$, which gives $121=2b+1$ and $b=60$. Check: $11^2+60^2=121+3600=3721=61^2$.

questions.stem: A right triangle with two equal legs has an area of 49 square centimeters. What is the square of the length of its hypotenuse?
questions.solution: Area $=\frac12\ell^2=49$, so $\ell^2=98$. The hypotenuse squared is $\ell^2+\ell^2=196$. (The hypotenuse is 14.)

questions.stem: A 45-45-90 triangle has a hypotenuse of $6\sqrt{2}$ centimeters. A line is drawn from the right angle straight down to the hypotenuse, meeting it at a right angle. How long is this line, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The legs are 6 centimeters each, so the area is $\frac12\times 6\times 6=18$. Using the hypotenuse as the base: $\frac12\times 6\sqrt2\times h=18$, so $h=\frac{6}{\sqrt2}=3\sqrt2$.

questions.stem: The diagonal of a square is 14 centimeters long. What is the area of the square, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: If the side is $s$, then $s^2+s^2=14^2=196$, so $s^2=98$. The area of the square is $s^2=98$ square centimeters.

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle is $5\sqrt{3}$ centimeters tall. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The height is the shortest side times $\sqrt3$, so half of the base is 5 and the side is 10 centimeters. The perimeter is $3\times 10=30$ centimeters.

questions.stem: What is the area of an equilateral triangle with sides of 6 centimeters, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The height is $3\sqrt3$ (a 30-60-90 triangle with shortest side 3). The area is $\frac12\times 6\times 3\sqrt3=9\sqrt3$.

questions.stem: A 30-60-90 triangle has an area of $8\sqrt{3}$ square centimeters. How long is its shortest side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: If the shortest side is $s$, the legs are $s$ and $s\sqrt3$, so the area is $\frac12 s^2\sqrt3=8\sqrt3$. Then $s^2=16$ and $s=4$ centimeters.

solve.work: Legs x and xsqrt3: x^2 sqrt3/2 = 8sqrt3 -> x^2 = 16, x = 4.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a diagonal of 20 centimeters. The diagonal makes a 30 degree angle with the longer side. What is the perimeter of the rectangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The diagonal and two sides form a 30-60-90 triangle with hypotenuse 20. The shorter side is 10 and the longer side is $10\sqrt3$. The perimeter is $2(10+10\sqrt3)=20+20\sqrt3$.

questions.stem: A 25-foot ladder leans against a wall with its foot 7 feet from the wall. The top of the ladder slides down the wall by 4 feet, and the ladder does not leave the wall or the ground. How many feet does the foot of the ladder move away from the wall?
questions.solution: At first the ladder reaches $\sqrt{625-49}=24$ feet up. After sliding 4 feet it reaches 20 feet, so the foot is now $\sqrt{625-400}=15$ feet from the wall. It has moved $15-7=8$ feet.

solve.work: Top at sqrt(625-49) = 24, slides to 20; foot sqrt(625-400) = 15; moves 15-7 = 8.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a diagonal of 26 centimeters and one side of 10 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The other side is $\sqrt{26^2-10^2}=\sqrt{576}=24$. The area is $10\times 24=240$ square centimeters.

questions.stem: A box is 3 centimeters wide, 4 centimeters deep and 12 centimeters tall. What is the distance from one bottom corner to the opposite top corner, straight through the inside of the box, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The diagonal across the bottom is $\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5$. This and the 12-centimeter edge are the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the distance wanted: $\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=\sqrt{169}=13$.

questions.stem: Two poles stand on level ground, 9 meters apart. One pole is 14 meters tall and the other is 2 meters tall. A straight rope is stretched from the top of one pole to the top of the other. How long is the rope, in meters?
questions.solution: The tops differ in height by $14-2=12$ meters, and are 9 meters apart across the ground. The rope is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 12 and 9: $\sqrt{144+81}=15$ meters.

questions.stem: The four angles of a quadrilateral are x, x + 10, x + 20 and x + 30 degrees. What is x?
questions.solution: The sum is $4x+60=360$, so $4x=300$ and $x=75$.

questions.stem: In parallelogram ABCD, the diagonals AC and BD cross at point E. AC is 20 centimeters long and BD is 14 centimeters long. What is the length AE + BE, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The diagonals of a parallelogram cut each other in half. So $AE=20\div 2=10$ and $BE=14\div 2=7$, and $AE+BE=17$.

questions.stem: ABCD is a rhombus and angle A is 50 degrees. The diagonal AC cuts angle A into two equal angles. How many degrees is angle CAB?
questions.solution: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect its angles, so angle CAB is half of 50: 25 degrees.

questions.stem: The two diagonals of a parallelogram have the same length. How many of the parallelogram's four angles are right angles?
questions.solution: Take one side of the parallelogram. The two diagonals and that side and the opposite side make two triangles that are the same shape and size, so the angles at the two ends of that side are equal. In a parallelogram those two angles also add to 180 degrees, so each is 90 degrees. All four angles are right angles (the shape is a rectangle).

solve.work: Equal diagonals make it a rectangle: 4 right angles.

questions.stem: An isosceles trapezoid has parallel sides of 10 centimeters and 20 centimeters, and each slanted side is 13 centimeters long. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The bases differ by 10, so each end sticks out 5. The height satisfies $5^2+h^2=13^2$, so $h=12$. Area $=\frac12\times(10+20)\times 12=180$.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has two right angles. Its parallel sides are 7 centimeters and 16 centimeters long, and its slanted side is 15 centimeters long. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The parallel sides differ by $16-7=9$. The slanted side is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with one leg 9, so the height is $\sqrt{225-81}=12$. Area $=\frac12\times(7+16)\times 12=138$.

solve.work: Right trapezoid: horizontal 16-7 = 9, slant 15, height 12. Area 23/2*12 = 138.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has sides of 8 centimeters and 12 centimeters, and the angle between them is 30 degrees. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Take the 12-centimeter side as the base. The height makes a 30-60-90 triangle with the 8-centimeter side as hypotenuse, so the height is half of 8, which is 4. Area $=12\times 4=48$.

questions.stem: A rhombus has diagonals of 10 centimeters and 24 centimeters. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The diagonals cross at right angles and cut each other in half, making right triangles with legs 5 and 12. Each side is $\sqrt{25+144}=13$. The perimeter is $4\times 13=52$.

questions.stem: The diagonals of a quadrilateral are equal in length and cut each other in half at right angles. What is the quadrilateral?
questions.solution: Diagonals that bisect each other make a parallelogram. Equal diagonals make it a rectangle. Perpendicular diagonals make it a rhombus. A shape that is both is a square.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a diagonal of 25 centimeters and a perimeter of 62 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The two sides add to $62\div 2=31$, and their squares add to $25^2=625$. Since $31^2=961=625+2ab$, we get $ab=168$. (The sides are 24 and 7.)

questions.stem: The midpoints of the four sides of a square with sides of 8 centimeters are joined in order to make a smaller square. What is the area of the smaller square, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each corner of the big square has a small right triangle cut off with legs 4 and 4, area 8. The four triangles total 32, so the smaller square has area $64-32=32$.

questions.stem: Five friends have 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 stickers. What is the mean number of stickers?
questions.solution: Add the numbers: $4+6+8+10+12=40$. Divide by how many numbers there are: $40\div5=8$.

questions.stem: What is the mean of the numbers 2, 3 and 10?
questions.solution: Add: $2+3+10=15$. There are 3 numbers, so the mean is $15\div3=5$. ($3$ is the median, $15$ is the sum and $8$ is the range.)

questions.stem: The high temperatures on four days were 12, 15, 18 and 15 degrees. What was the mean high temperature, in degrees?
questions.solution: The sum is $12+15+18+15=60$. The mean is $60\div4=15$.

questions.stem: What is the median of 3, 9, 5, 7 and 1?
questions.solution: Put the numbers in order: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The middle number is 5.

questions.stem: What is the median of 11, 3 and 4?
questions.solution: In order the numbers are 3, 4, 11. The middle one is 4. ($3$ is the middle number as listed, but the list has to be put in order first. $6$ is the mean and $8$ is the range.)

questions.stem: Five students are 130, 125, 140, 128 and 135 centimeters tall. What is the median height, in centimeters?
questions.solution: In order: 125, 128, 130, 135, 140. The middle height is 130.

questions.stem: What is the mode of 3, 5, 5, 7 and 2?
questions.solution: The mode is the number that appears most often. 5 appears twice and the others once, so the mode is 5.

questions.stem: The shoe sizes in a group are 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 8 and 9. What is the mode of the sizes?
questions.solution: Size 8 appears three times, more than any other size. So the mode is 8. ($3$ is how many times it appears, not the mode.)

questions.stem: Six children read 10, 12, 10, 15, 12 and 10 pages. What is the mode of these numbers?
questions.solution: 10 appears three times, 12 twice and 15 once. The mode is 10.

questions.stem: The numbers are 4, 9, 15 and 2. What is their range?
questions.solution: The range is the largest number minus the smallest: $15-2=13$.

questions.stem: One day the highest temperature was 18 degrees and the lowest was 7 degrees. What is the range of the temperatures that day, in degrees?
questions.solution: The range is highest minus lowest: $18-7=11$. ($25$ is the sum and $12.5$ is halfway between the two.)

questions.stem: Four friends are 11, 14, 9 and 13 years old. What is the range of their ages, in years?
questions.solution: The oldest is 14 and the youngest is 9, so the range is $14-9=5$ years.

questions.skill: Missing value for a given mean
questions.stem: The mean of 4, 6 and ? is 6. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Three numbers with mean 6 have sum $3\times6=18$. So ? $=18-4-6=8$.

questions.skill: Missing value for a given mean
questions.stem: The mean of four numbers is 5. Three of the numbers are 2, 5 and 6. What is the fourth number?
questions.solution: Four numbers with mean 5 have sum $4\times5=20$. The three known numbers add to 13, so the fourth is $20-13=7$.

questions.skill: Missing value for a given mean
questions.stem: Mia scored 8 and 10 on two quizzes. What score on a third quiz gives her a mean of 9 for the three quizzes?
questions.solution: A mean of 9 over three quizzes means a total of 27. So far she has 18, so she needs $27-18=9$.

questions.stem: A farmer picked a mean of 7 apples from each of 4 trees. How many apples did the farmer pick in all?
questions.solution: Total = mean times how many: $7\times4=28$ apples.

questions.stem: A team scored a mean of 3 goals per game over 6 games. How many goals did the team score in all?
questions.solution: Total = mean times number of games: $3\times6=18$ goals.

questions.stem: Eight numbers have a sum of 56. What is their mean?
questions.solution: The mean is the sum divided by how many numbers: $56\div8=7$.

questions.stem: Ten pears in one basket have a mean mass of 5 ounces. Ten pears in another basket have a mean mass of 9 ounces. What is the mean mass of all 20 pears, in ounces?
questions.solution: The groups are the same size, so the mean of all is halfway between 5 and 9. Check: total $50+90=140$ ounces, and $140\div20=7$.

questions.stem: Two numbers have a sum of 12. Three other numbers have a sum of 18. What is the mean of all five numbers?
questions.solution: All five numbers have sum $12+18=30$. The mean is $30\div5=6$.

questions.stem: Three pencils cost a mean of 20 cents each and three pens cost a mean of 30 cents each. What is the mean cost of all six items, in cents?
questions.solution: The pencils cost $3\times20=60$ cents and the pens $3\times30=90$ cents, a total of 150 cents. For six items the mean is $150\div6=25$ cents.

questions.skill: How changing the data changes the mean
questions.stem: The numbers 4, 6 and 8 have a mean of 6. Each number is increased by 3. What is the new mean?
questions.solution: Adding 3 to every number adds 3 to the total of each one, so the mean goes up by 3: $6+3=9$. (Check: 7, 9, 11 have mean 9.)

solve.work: Adding 3 to each raises mean by 3: 9.

questions.skill: How changing the data changes the mean
questions.stem: Every number in a list is doubled. What happens to the mean of the list?
questions.solution: Doubling every number doubles their sum. The number of values is unchanged, so the mean is doubled too. (Try 2, 4, 6: the mean is 4. Doubled: 4, 8, 12, with mean 8.)

solve.work: Mean scales with the numbers: doubled.

questions.skill: How changing the data changes the mean
questions.stem: Five numbers have a mean of 20. One of them, 12, is changed to 17. What is the new mean?
questions.solution: The total was $5\times20=100$. Changing 12 to 17 adds 5, so the total is 105. The new mean is $105\div5=21$.

questions.stem: Three test scores of 70, 80 and 90 have a mean of 80. A fourth score of 100 is added. What is the new mean?
questions.solution: The four scores total $70+80+90+100=340$. The new mean is $340\div4=85$.

questions.stem: The median of 2, 4, 8, 10 and 11 is 8. A sixth number, 12, is added to the list. What is the median of the six numbers?
questions.solution: Now the list 2, 4, 8, 10, 11, 12 has six numbers. The median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th, 8 and 10: $(8+10)\div2=9$.

questions.stem: The median of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 is 5. The number 9 is removed. What is the median of the four numbers left?
questions.solution: The four numbers left are 1, 3, 5, 7. The median is halfway between the middle two: $(3+5)\div2=4$.

questions.skill: Comparing mean, median, mode and range
questions.stem: Which of these tells how spread out a list of numbers is, from the smallest to the largest?
questions.solution: The range is the largest number minus the smallest, so it measures the spread. The mean, median and mode describe the middle or the most common value.

solve.work: Spread from smallest to largest is the range.

questions.skill: Comparing mean, median, mode and range
questions.stem: Which of these is found by adding all the numbers and then dividing by how many numbers there are?
questions.solution: Adding the numbers and dividing by how many there are gives the mean. The median is the middle number in order, the mode is the most common, and the range is largest minus smallest.

solve.work: Sum divided by count is the mean.

questions.skill: Comparing mean, median, mode and range
questions.stem: For the list 3, 3, 6, 9, 14, what is the range minus the mode?
questions.solution: The range is $14-3=11$. The mode is 3, because it appears twice. So the answer is $11-3=8$.

questions.stem: Two baskets hold 3 apples each and two baskets hold 5 apples each. What is the mean number of apples per basket?
questions.solution: The total is $3+3+5+5=16$ apples in 4 baskets. The mean is $16\div4=4$.

questions.stem: Of 9 houses, 4 have 1 pet, 3 have 2 pets and 2 have 3 pets. What is the median number of pets?
questions.solution: In order the numbers of pets are 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3. The middle (5th) number is 2.

questions.stem: Of 16 children, 7 have 2 pets, 4 have 1 pet, 3 have 3 pets and 2 have no pets. What is the mode of the number of pets?
questions.solution: The most common number of pets is 2 (7 children). So the mode is 2. ($7$ is how many children have that number, not the mode.)

questions.stem: Ana scored 78, 85, 92, 90 and 80 on five tests. What is her mean score?
What is the mean of 3, 4, 4 and 6?
questions.solution: The sum is $3+4+4+6=17$. The mean is $17\div4=4.25$. ($4$ is the median and the mode, $4.5$ is halfway between the smallest and the largest, and $17$ is the sum.)

questions.stem: A bakery sold 14, 9, 21, 18, 8 and 20 muffins on six days. What is the mean number of muffins sold per day?
questions.solution: The total is $14+9+21+18+8+20=90$ muffins. Divide by 6 days: $90\div6=15$.

questions.stem: What is the median of 4, 8, 10, 15, 20 and 3?
questions.solution: In order: 3, 4, 8, 10, 15, 20. There are six numbers, so the median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th: $(8+10)\div2=9$.

questions.stem: What is the median of 2, 3, 5, 8, 10 and 30?
questions.solution: The list is already in order and has six numbers. The median is halfway between the two middle numbers, 5 and 8: $(5+8)\div2=6.5$. ($16$ is halfway between the smallest and the largest.)

questions.stem: Seven children read 0, 3, 3, 5, 2, 8 and 1 books last month. What is the median number of books?
questions.solution: In order: 0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 5, 8. The middle (4th) number is 3.

questions.stem: In the list 3, 7, 7, 4, 4, 9, x the number x is chosen so that the list has just one mode, and that mode is 4. What is x?
questions.solution: Right now 7 and 4 both appear twice. To make 4 the only mode, 4 must appear a third time, so x is 4.

solve.work: Without x: 7 twice, 4 twice. For 4 to be the only mode, x=4 (then 4 thrice).

questions.stem: Which of these lists has more than one mode?
questions.solution: In $2,2,5,7,7,9$ both 2 and 7 appear twice, so there are two modes. In the others, 4 appears most (three times), 3 appears most, and 6 appears most: one mode each.

solve.work: A: 2 and 7 each twice -> two modes. B: 3. C: 4 (three times). D: 6. A.

questions.stem: Five plants are 142, 138, 151, 147 and 139 centimeters tall. What is the range of their heights, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The tallest is 151 and the shortest is 138. The range is $151-138=13$ centimeters.

questions.stem: Which of these lists has the greatest range?
questions.solution: The ranges are: $40-5=35$; $60-30=30$; $120-90=30$; $41-7=34$. The greatest is 35, from $5,40,22,18$. Big numbers do not make a big range: only the gap between largest and smallest matters.

questions.stem: The range of five scores is 18. The lowest score is 62. What is the highest score?
questions.solution: Range = highest minus lowest, so highest = lowest plus range: $62+18=80$.

questions.skill: Missing value for a given mean
questions.stem: Dev scored 82, 90, 76 and 88 on four tests. What score on the fifth test would give him a mean of exactly 85 over the five tests?
questions.solution: Five tests with mean 85 total $5\times85=425$. The first four total 336, so the fifth must be $425-336=89$.

questions.skill: Missing value for a given mean
questions.stem: Six numbers have a mean of 11. Five of them are 9, 14, 10, 12 and 8. What is the sixth number?
questions.solution: The six numbers total $6\times11=66$. The five known numbers total 53, so the sixth is $66-53=13$.

questions.skill: Missing value for a given mean
questions.stem: Three friends have a mean height of 150 centimeters. Two of them are 148 and 155 centimeters tall. How tall is the third friend, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The total height is $3\times150=450$. The two known heights total 303, so the third friend is $450-303=147$ centimeters tall.

questions.stem: The mean height of 12 players is 150 centimeters. What is the total of their 12 heights, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Total = mean times how many: $150\times12=1800$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A bakery made a mean of 48 loaves a day for 6 days. How many loaves must it make on the 7th day so that the total over the 7 days is 350?
questions.solution: In 6 days it made $6\times48=288$ loaves. It needs $350-288=62$ more on the 7th day.

questions.stem: Rain fell on 5 days with a mean of 6 millimeters per day. On a sixth day, 4 more millimeters fell. How many millimeters fell in total over the six days?
questions.solution: The first five days gave $5\times6=30$ millimeters. Add the sixth day: $30+4=34$.

questions.stem: Two classes took the same test. The 20 students in class P had a mean score of 80. The 30 students in class Q had a mean score of 90. What was the mean score of all 50 students?
questions.solution: Class P total: $20\times80=1600$. Class Q total: $30\times90=2700$. All together: $4300$. Divide by 50: $4300\div50=86$.

questions.stem: Four boys have a mean weight of 150 pounds. Six girls have a mean weight of 140 pounds. What is the mean weight of all ten children, in pounds?
questions.solution: The boys weigh $4\times150=600$ pounds and the girls $6\times140=840$ pounds. Together that is 1440 pounds, so the mean is $1440\div10=144$ pounds.

questions.stem: The mean of 3 numbers is 12 and the mean of 2 other numbers is 17. What is the mean of all five numbers?
questions.solution: The first three total $3\times12=36$ and the other two total $2\times17=34$. All five total 70, so the mean is $70\div5=14$. (The mean is not halfway between 12 and 17, because the groups are different sizes.)

questions.skill: How changing the data changes the mean
questions.stem: Eight numbers have a mean of 25. One of them, 40, is replaced by 24. What is the new mean?
questions.solution: The total was $8\times25=200$. Replacing 40 by 24 takes away 16, so the total is 184. The new mean is $184\div8=23$.

questions.skill: How changing the data changes the mean
questions.stem: A list of numbers has a mean of 5. Each number is multiplied by 3, and then 2 is subtracted from the result. What is the mean of the new list?
questions.solution: Multiplying every number by 3 multiplies the mean by 3, giving 15. Subtracting 2 from every number lowers the mean by 2, giving $15-2=13$.

questions.skill: How changing the data changes the mean
questions.stem: Six numbers have a mean of 30. One of the numbers is increased by 12 and another is decreased by 6. What is the new mean?
questions.solution: The total was $6\times30=180$. The changes add $12-6=6$ to the total, which becomes 186. The new mean is $186\div6=31$.

questions.stem: The mean of six numbers is 15. One of them, 25, is removed. What is the mean of the five numbers left?
questions.solution: The six numbers total $6\times15=90$. Without 25 the total is 65, and the mean of five numbers is $65\div5=13$.

questions.stem: The mean of five scores is 80. A sixth score of 92 is added. What is the mean of all six scores?
questions.solution: The first five total $5\times80=400$. With 92 the total is 492, and $492\div6=82$. (86 is halfway between 80 and 92, which ignores that 80 stands for five scores.)

questions.stem: The seven numbers 2, 5, 9, 14, 20, 21 and 30 have a median of 14. The number 1 is added to the list. What is the new median?
questions.solution: The eight numbers in order are 1, 2, 5, 9, 14, 20, 21, 30. The median is halfway between the 4th and 5th: $(9+14)\div2=11.5$.

questions.skill: Comparing mean, median, mode and range
questions.stem: For the list 4, 5, 5, 6, 40, how much larger is the mean than the median?
questions.solution: The mean is $(4+5+5+6+40)\div5=60\div5=12$. The median (middle number) is 5. The mean is $12-5=7$ larger.

questions.skill: Comparing mean, median, mode and range
questions.stem: Which statement is true for the list 2, 3, 3, 4, 18?
choices: The median is greater than the mean
The mode is greater than the median
The mean is greater than the median
The range is smaller than the mean
questions.answer: The mean is greater than the median
questions.solution: The mean is $30\div5=6$, the median is 3, the mode is 3 and the range is $18-2=16$. Only "the mean is greater than the median" is true: the large number 18 pulls the mean up but not the median.

solve.answer: The mean is greater than the median
solve.work: Mean 30/5=6, median 3, mode 3, range 16. A true; B false (16>6); C false; D false (3=3).

questions.skill: Comparing mean, median, mode and range
questions.stem: For the list 10, 12, 12, 14, 22, what is the sum of the mean, the median and the mode?
questions.solution: The mean is $70\div5=14$. The median is 12 and the mode is 12. The sum is $14+12+12=38$.

questions.stem: Among 10 students, 3 wear size 5 shoes, 5 wear size 6 and 2 wear size 7. What is the mean shoe size?
questions.solution: The sizes total $3\times5+5\times6+2\times7=15+30+14=59$. The mean is $59\div10=5.9$.

questions.stem: In a quiz of 20 students, 2 scored 1 point, 4 scored 2 points, 5 scored 3 points, 5 scored 4 points and 4 scored 5 points. What is the median score?
questions.solution: With 20 scores, the median is halfway between the 10th and 11th. Counting up: 2 scores of 1, then 4 of 2 (6 so far), then 5 of 3 (11 so far). So both the 10th and the 11th score are 3, and the median is 3.

solve.work: Cumulative: score1 2, score2 6, score3 11; 10th and 11th are both 3; median 3.

questions.stem: A jar holds 4 coins worth 5 cents, 3 coins worth 10 cents and 3 coins worth 20 cents. What is the mean value of a coin, in cents?
questions.solution: The coins total $20+30+60=110$ cents. There are 10 coins, so the mean is $110\div10=11$ cents.

questions.stem: What is the mean of all the whole numbers from 1 to 49?
questions.solution: The numbers are evenly spread, so the mean is halfway between the smallest and the largest: $(1+49)\div2=25$. (Pairing 1 with 49, 2 with 48, and so on, gives pairs that each add to 50, so the middle number 25 is the mean.)

questions.stem: What is the mean of 97, 98, 99, 100, 101, 102 and 103?
questions.solution: Each number is some distance from 100: $-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3$. These distances cancel to 0, so the mean is exactly 100.

questions.stem: What is the mean of 1.2, 0.8, 2.5 and 1.5?
questions.solution: The sum is $1.2+0.8+2.5+1.5=6$. Divide by 4: $6\div4=1.5$. ($1.35$ is the median, $6$ is the sum and $1.7$ is the range.)

questions.stem: Five different numbers have a median of 12. Four of them are 5, 9, 20 and 31. What is the fifth number?
questions.solution: The median of five numbers is the 3rd in order. With 5, 9, 20, 31 already there, the fifth number must go between 9 and 20 to be 3rd. Then it is the median itself, so it is 12.

solve.work: Sorted known: 5,9,20,31. Median of five is the 3rd. If the fifth number were below 9 the median would be 9; above 20 it would be 20; between 9 and 20 it is the fifth number itself, so it must be 12 (different from the others, ok).

questions.stem: Which of these lists has a median of 6?
questions.solution: Put each list in order. $1,3,6,7,9$ has middle number 6. $2,4,6,8$ has median $5$. $1,2,3,6,10$ has median $3$. $1,2,3,6,9,11$ has median $4.5$. Only the first list has median 6.

questions.stem: The numbers 4, 9, 15, 2, 11 and x are listed, where x is a whole number bigger than 15. What is the median of the six numbers?
questions.solution: Since x is bigger than 15, the order is 2, 4, 9, 11, 15, x. The median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th numbers: $(9+11)\div2=10$. It does not matter which number x is.

questions.stem: The list 3, 8, 3, 5, 8, n, 5 has seven numbers. What whole number n makes 8 the only mode of the list?
questions.solution: At the moment 3, 8 and 5 each appear twice. If n is 8, then 8 appears three times and is the only mode. Any other n would leave a tie or make n a mode.

solve.work: 3, 8, 5 each appear twice. n=8 makes 8 appear three times, the only mode.

questions.stem: Each of the whole numbers from 1 to 10 is divided by 3, and the ten remainders are listed. What is the mode of the remainders?
questions.solution: The remainders are 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0, 1. Remainder 1 appears 4 times, and 0 and 2 appear 3 times each. The mode is 1.

solve.work: Remainders for 1..10: 1,2,0,1,2,0,1,2,0,1. Count: 1 four times, 2 and 0 three times. Mode 1.

questions.stem: Which list has a mean of 6, a median of 5 and a mode of 4?
questions.solution: The list $4,4,5,8,9$ has sum 30, so the mean is 6; its middle number is 5 and 4 appears twice. The list $4,5,5,7,9$ has mode 5. The list $4,4,6,7,9$ has median 6. The list $3,4,4,5,9$ has mean 5.

solve.work: A: sum 30 mean 6, median 5, mode 5 (no). B: 4,4,5,8,9 sum 30 mean 6, median 5, mode 4 (yes). C: median 6. D: sum 25 mean 5. B.

questions.stem: The range of the numbers 3, 15, x, 8, 11 and 6 is 20, and x is bigger than all the other numbers. What is x?
questions.solution: The smallest number is 3, and x is the largest. Largest minus smallest is 20, so $x=3+20=23$.

questions.stem: What is the smallest possible range of a list of five different whole numbers?
questions.solution: The closest five different whole numbers are consecutive, such as 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Their range is $5-1=4$. Any other five different whole numbers are at least as spread out.

solve.work: Five different whole numbers: consecutive like 1..5 give range 4; any five distinct integers span at least 4.

questions.stem: In one week the hottest day was 3 degrees more than twice the temperature of the coolest day. The range of the week's temperatures was 14 degrees. What was the hottest temperature, in degrees?
questions.solution: If the coolest day was c degrees, the hottest was $2c+3$. The range is $(2c+3)-c=c+3=14$, so $c=11$. The hottest day was $2\times11+3=25$ degrees.

questions.skill: Missing value for a given mean
questions.stem: After 5 games a player had scored a mean of 14 points per game. What mean number of points must the player score over the next 3 games so that the mean over all 8 games is 17?
questions.solution: After 8 games the total must be $8\times17=136$. The first 5 games gave $5\times14=70$. The last 3 games must give $136-70=66$, a mean of $66\div3=22$.

solve.work: Total needed 8*17=136; have 5*14=70; next 3 games total 66, mean 22.

questions.skill: Missing value for a given mean
questions.stem: Five numbers have a mean of 20. The largest is 36, and the other four are all equal. What is each of the other four?
questions.solution: The total is $5\times20=100$. Without 36, the other four total 64, so each is $64\div4=16$.

questions.skill: Missing value for a given mean
questions.stem: The mean of five test scores is 84. When the highest score is removed, the mean of the other four is 80. What was the highest score?
questions.solution: The five scores total $5\times84=420$. The four others total $4\times80=320$. The highest is $420-320=100$.

questions.stem: Seven numbers have a mean of 18. The mean of the first four is 15 and the mean of the last four is 21. (The fourth number is in both groups.) What is the fourth number?
questions.solution: The seven numbers total $7\times18=126$. The first four total 60 and the last four total 84, so together $60+84=144$. This counts the fourth number twice, so it is $144-126=18$.

solve.work: Total 7*18=126. First four sum 60, last four sum 84; 60+84=144 counts the fourth twice, so fourth = 144-126=18.

questions.stem: Seven numbers have a mean of 9. Three of them have a mean of 5. What is the mean of the other four?
questions.solution: The seven numbers total $7\times9=63$. The three total $3\times5=15$. The other four total $63-15=48$, so their mean is $48\div4=12$.

solve.work: Total 63; three sum 15; other four 48; mean 12.

questions.stem: The sum of a list of numbers is 132, and their mean is 12. How many numbers are in the list?
questions.solution: Mean = sum divided by how many, so how many = sum divided by mean: $132\div12=11$.

questions.stem: In a class the mean test score is 78. The 12 girls have a mean score of 80 and the boys have a mean score of 75. How many boys are in the class?
questions.solution: Let b be the number of boys. Total points: $75b+80\times12=78(b+12)$, so $75b+960=78b+936$. Then $3b=24$ and $b=8$. Check: $600+960=1560$ and $1560\div20=78$.

questions.stem: Six numbers have a mean of 10. Some other numbers have a mean of 20. All the numbers together have a mean of 16. How many other numbers are there?
questions.solution: Let n be the number of other numbers. Then $60+20n=16(6+n)=96+16n$, so $4n=36$ and $n=9$. Check: $60+180=240$ and $240\div15=16$.

questions.stem: The mean of 15 numbers is 8. Ten more numbers are added. The mean of all 25 numbers is 10. What is the mean of the ten new numbers?
questions.solution: All 25 numbers total $25\times10=250$. The first 15 total $15\times8=120$. The ten new numbers total $250-120=130$, so their mean is $130\div10=13$.

questions.skill: How changing the data changes the mean
questions.stem: Nine numbers were found to have a mean of 22, but one of them was read as 35 when it should have been 53. What is the correct mean?
questions.solution: The total with the mistake was $9\times22=198$. Replacing 35 by 53 adds 18, so the correct total is 216. The correct mean is $216\div9=24$.

questions.skill: How changing the data changes the mean
questions.stem: A list of numbers has a mean of 40. One of the numbers is increased by 30, and the mean becomes 43. How many numbers are in the list?
questions.solution: Increasing one number by 30 adds 30 to the total. That raises the mean by 3, so $30\div n=3$ and $n=10$.

solve.work: Mean rises 3 when sum rises 30: 30/n=3, n=10.

questions.skill: How changing the data changes the mean
questions.stem: A list of 4 numbers has a mean of 10. Each number is replaced by three times itself minus 4. What is the sum of the new numbers?
questions.solution: The new mean is $3\times10-4=26$. With 4 numbers, the sum is $4\times26=104$. ($116$ forgets to take 4 off each of the four numbers.)

questions.stem: The mean of five numbers is 12. A sixth number, x, is added, and the mean of the six numbers is 14. What is x?
questions.solution: The five numbers total $5\times12=60$. The six total $6\times14=84$. So $x=84-60=24$.

questions.stem: Six numbers have a mean of 20. Two of them, which add up to 50, are removed. What is the mean of the four numbers left?
questions.solution: The six numbers total $6\times20=120$. Taking away 50 leaves 70, shared among 4 numbers: $70\div4=17.5$.

questions.stem: Taru scored a mean of 78 on four quizzes. What score on a fifth quiz would raise her mean for the five quizzes by exactly 2?
questions.solution: The new mean must be 80. Five quizzes then total $5\times80=400$. The first four total $4\times78=312$. So the fifth score is $400-312=88$.

questions.skill: Comparing mean, median, mode and range
questions.stem: Which of these lists has a mean of 7, a median of 6 and a mode of 5?
questions.solution: All four lists have sum 35, so the mean is 7 in each. $5,5,6,9,10$ has median 6 and mode 5. $5,6,6,8,10$ has mode 6. $5,5,7,8,10$ has median 7. $4,5,6,9,11$ has no repeated number, so no mode of 5.

solve.work: All sum 35 (mean 7). A median 6 but no mode. B median 7. C mode 6. D: 5,5,6,9,10 median 6, mode 5. D.

questions.skill: Comparing mean, median, mode and range
questions.stem: Five different positive whole numbers have a mean of 6 and a median of 5. What is the greatest value that the largest of the five numbers could have?
questions.solution: The numbers total $5\times6=30$ and the middle one is 5. To make the largest as big as possible, make the other three as small as possible: the two below 5 are 1 and 2, and the one just above 5 is 6. The largest is then $30-5-1-2-6=16$.

questions.skill: Comparing mean, median, mode and range
questions.stem: Four whole numbers have a mean of 5, a median of 4 and a mode of 3. What is the largest of the four numbers?
questions.solution: The numbers total $4\times5=20$. The mode 3 must appear at least twice, and they are the two smallest, so the list starts 3, 3. The median is halfway between the 2nd and 3rd: $(3+x)\div2=4$, so the 3rd number is 5. The largest is $20-3-3-5=9$. The list 3, 3, 5, 9 works.

solve.work: Sum 20, sorted a<=b<=c<=d, b+c=8, mode 3. 3 must appear at least twice and more than any other; b=c=4 would allow only one 3. So a=b=3, c=5, d=20-11=9. Check 3,3,5,9: mean 5, median 4, mode 3.

questions.stem: In a test, 6 students scored 70, 4 students scored 80 and the rest scored 90. The mean score of all the students was 80. How many students scored 90?
A survey of families found that 3 had 1 child, 4 had 2 children, some had 3 children and 1 had 4 children. The mean number of children per family was 2.25. How many families had 3 children?
questions.solution: Let k families have 3 children. Total children: $3+8+3k+4=15+3k$ for $8+k$ families. So $15+3k=2.25(8+k)=18+2.25k$, giving $0.75k=3$ and $k=4$. Check: $27\div12=2.25$.

questions.stem: In a list of 12 numbers, 5 appears 4 times, 7 appears 5 times and 9 appears 3 times. Which statement is true?
choices: The mean is above 7, and the median and the mode are both 7
The mean and the median are both 7, and the mode is 5
The mean is below 7, the median is 6, and the mode is 7
The mean is below 7, and the median and the mode are both 7
questions.answer: The mean is below 7, and the median and the mode are both 7
questions.solution: The total is $20+35+27=82$, so the mean is $82\div12\approx6.8$, below 7. In order, the 6th and 7th numbers are both 7, so the median is 7. The mode is 7, which appears 5 times.

solve.answer: The mean is below 7, and the median and the mode are both 7
solve.work: Sum 20+35+27=82; mean 82/12 about 6.83 < 7. Sorted: four 5s, five 7s, three 9s; 6th and 7th are 7, median 7; mode 7. A.

questions.stem: A cafe has 3 kinds of sandwich and 4 kinds of drink. A lunch is one sandwich and one drink. How many different lunches are there?
questions.solution: Each of the 3 sandwiches can go with any of the 4 drinks, so there are $3\times4=12$ lunches.

questions.stem: Lena has 5 shirts and 2 pairs of shorts. An outfit is one shirt and one pair of shorts. How many different outfits can she make?
questions.solution: Each of the 5 shirts can be worn with either pair of shorts: $5\times2=10$ outfits. ($7$ comes from adding instead of multiplying.)

questions.stem: There are 4 roads from town A to town B and 5 roads from town B to town C. How many different ways can you drive from A to C, going through B?
questions.solution: For each of the 4 roads to B there are 5 roads on to C: $4\times5=20$ ways.

questions.stem: How many two-digit numbers can be made using only the digits 1, 2 and 3, if a digit may be used twice (like 22)?
questions.solution: There are 3 choices for the tens digit and 3 for the ones digit: $3\times3=9$.

solve.work: 3 choices for each of two digits: 9.

questions.stem: A code has 3 digits. Each digit is either 0 or 1. How many different codes are there?
questions.solution: There are 2 choices for each of the 3 digits: $2\times2\times2=8$.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers are there from 10 to 99, counting both 10 and 99?
questions.solution: The count is the last minus the first, plus 1: $99-10+1=90$.

questions.stem: How many two-digit numbers have digits that add up to 3?
questions.solution: List by the tens digit: 12, 21 and 30. That is 3 numbers.

questions.stem: A bakery sells 3 kinds of pie and 5 kinds of cake. Jo buys either one pie or one cake, but not both. How many different choices does she have?
questions.solution: Either she picks a pie (3 ways) or a cake (5 ways). These cases do not overlap, so add: $3+5=8$.

questions.stem: In how many ways can two whole numbers, both bigger than 0, add up to 5, if the order counts (so 1 + 4 and 4 + 1 are different)?
questions.solution: The pairs are 1 + 4, 2 + 3, 3 + 2 and 4 + 1. That is 4 ways.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 20 are not multiples of 5?
questions.solution: There are 20 numbers. The multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15, 20: 4 of them. So $20-4=16$ are not.

questions.stem: A bag has 12 different marbles, and 5 of them are red. In how many ways can you pick one marble that is not red?
questions.solution: Of the 12 marbles, 5 are red, so $12-5=7$ are not red. That is 7 ways.

questions.stem: How many two-digit numbers are not multiples of 10?
questions.solution: There are 90 two-digit numbers. The multiples of 10 are 10, 20, ..., 90: 9 of them. $90-9=81$.

questions.stem: Three friends stand in a line for a photo. In how many different orders can they stand?
questions.solution: 3 choices for who is first, then 2, then 1: $3\times2\times1=6$.

questions.stem: Four different books are placed in a row on a shelf. In how many different orders can this be done?
questions.solution: 4 choices for the first book, 3 for the next, 2 for the next and 1 for the last: $4\times3\times2\times1=24$.

questions.stem: Using each of the digits 1, 2 and 3 exactly once, how many different 3-digit numbers can be made?
questions.solution: 3 choices for the hundreds digit, 2 for the tens and 1 for the ones: $3\times2\times1=6$. (They are 123, 132, 213, 231, 312, 321.)

questions.stem: Ann, Bo and Cy stand in a line. Ann must be first. In how many different orders can they stand?
questions.solution: Ann is first. Bo and Cy fill the other 2 places in $2\times1=2$ ways: Ann Bo Cy and Ann Cy Bo.

solve.work: Ann fixed first; the other two in 2 orders.

questions.stem: Four students line up, and the tallest student must stand at the front. In how many different orders can they line up?
questions.solution: The tallest student is first. The other 3 students fill the remaining places in $3\times2\times1=6$ ways.

questions.stem: Using each of the digits 1, 2 and 3 exactly once, how many of the 3-digit numbers that can be made are even?
questions.solution: An even number must end in 2. The other two digits, 1 and 3, can go in front in 2 orders: 132 and 312.

solve.work: Even means last digit 2; the other two digits in 2 orders: 2.

questions.stem: A club of 5 members chooses a president, then a secretary who must be a different member. In how many ways can they do this?
questions.solution: 5 choices for president, then 4 for secretary: $5\times4=20$.

questions.stem: Four runners are in a race, with no ties. Gold goes to the first runner and silver to the second. In how many ways can the gold and silver medals be given out?
questions.solution: 4 runners could win gold. Then 3 are left for silver. $4\times3=12$. ($6$ would count each pair once, ignoring who gets which medal.)

questions.stem: A teacher picks one of 6 children to lead the line and a different child to hold the door. In how many ways can she choose?
questions.solution: 6 choices for the line leader, then 5 for the door holder: $6\times5=30$.

questions.skill: Choosing a group (order does not matter)
questions.stem: A snack is 2 different fruits chosen from an apple, a banana, a cherry and a date. The order does not matter. How many different snacks are there?
questions.solution: With order, there would be $4\times3=12$ choices. Each snack is counted twice (apple then banana is the same as banana then apple). $12\div2=6$.

questions.skill: Choosing a group (order does not matter)
